     1	/**
     2	 * @class
     3	 * @private
     4	 */
     5	function PriorityQueue (size) {
     6	  if (!(this instanceof PriorityQueue)) {
     7	    return new PriorityQueue()
     8	  }
     9	
    10	  this._size = size
    11	  this._slots = null
    12	  this._total = null
    13	
    14	  // initialize arrays to hold queue elements
    15	  size = Math.max(+size | 0, 1)
    16	  this._slots = []
    17	  for (var i = 0; i < size; i += 1) {
    18	    this._slots.push([])
    19	  }
    20	}
    21	
    22	PriorityQueue.prototype.size = function size () {
    23	  if (this._total === null) {
    24	    this._total = 0
    25	    for (var i = 0; i < this._size; i += 1) {
    26	      this._total += this._slots[i].length
    27	    }
    28	  }
    29	  return this._total
    30	}
    31	
    32	PriorityQueue.prototype.enqueue = function enqueue (obj, priority) {
    33	  var priorityOrig
    34	
    35	  // Convert to integer with a default value of 0.
    36	  priority = priority && +priority | 0 || 0
    37	
    38	  // Clear cache for total.
    39	  this._total = null
    40	  if (priority) {
    41	    priorityOrig = priority
    42	    if (priority < 0 || priority >= this._size) {
    43	      priority = (this._size - 1)
    44	      // put obj at the end of the line
    45	      console.error('invalid priority: ' + priorityOrig + ' must be between 0 and ' + priority)
    46	    }
    47	  }
    48	
    49	  this._slots[priority].push(obj)
    50	}
    51	
    52	PriorityQueue.prototype.dequeue = function dequeue (callback) {
    53	  var obj = null
    54	  // Clear cache for total.
    55	  this._total = null
    56	  for (var i = 0, sl = this._slots.length; i < sl; i += 1) {
    57	    if (this._slots[i].length) {
    58	      obj = this._slots[i].shift()
    59	      break
    60	    }
    61	  }
    62	  return obj
    63	}
    64	
    65	function doWhileAsync (conditionFn, iterateFn, callbackFn) {
    66	  var next = function () {
    67	    if (conditionFn()) {
    68	      iterateFn(next)
    69	    } else {
    70	      callbackFn()
    71	    }
    72	  }
    73	  next()
    74	}
    75	
    76	/**
    77	 * Generate an Object pool with a specified `factory`.
    78	 *
    79	 * @class
    80	 * @param {Object} factory
    81	 *   Factory to be used for generating and destorying the items.
    82	 * @param {String} factory.name
    83	 *   Name of the factory. Serves only logging purposes.
    84	 * @param {Function} factory.create
    85	 *   Should create the item to be acquired,
    86	 *   and call it's first callback argument with the generated item as it's argument.
    87	 * @param {Function} factory.destroy
    88	 *   Should gently close any resources that the item is using.
    89	 *   Called before the items is destroyed.
    90	 * @param {Function} factory.validate
    91	 *   Should return true if connection is still valid and false
    92	 *   If it should be removed from pool. Called before item is
    93	 *   acquired from pool.
    94	 * @param {Function} factory.validateAsync
    95	 *   Asynchronous validate function. Receives a callback function
    96	 *   as its second argument, that should be called with a single
    97	 *   boolean argument being true if the item is still valid and false
    98	 *   if it should be removed from pool. Called before item is
    99	 *   acquired from pool. Only one of validate/validateAsync may be specified
   100	 * @param {Number} factory.max
   101	 *   Maximum number of items that can exist at the same time.  Default: 1.
   102	 *   Any further acquire requests will be pushed to the waiting list.
   103	 * @param {Number} factory.min
   104	 *   Minimum number of items in pool (including in-use). Default: 0.
   105	 *   When the pool is created, or a resource destroyed, this minimum will
   106	 *   be checked. If the pool resource count is below the minimum, a new
   107	 *   resource will be created and added to the pool.
   108	 * @param {Number} factory.idleTimeoutMillis
   109	 *   Delay in milliseconds after the idle items in the pool will be destroyed.
   110	 *   And idle item is that is not acquired yet. Waiting items doesn't count here.
   111	 * @param {Number} factory.reapIntervalMillis
   112	 *   Cleanup is scheduled in every `factory.reapIntervalMillis` milliseconds.
   113	 * @param {Boolean|Function} factory.log
   114	 *   Whether the pool should log activity. If function is specified,
   115	 *   that will be used instead. The function expects the arguments msg, loglevel
   116	 * @param {Number} factory.priorityRange
   117	 *   The range from 1 to be treated as a valid priority
   118	 * @param {RefreshIdle} factory.refreshIdle
   119	 *   Should idle resources be destroyed and recreated every idleTimeoutMillis? Default: true.
   120	 * @param {Bool} [factory.returnToHead=false]
   121	 *   Returns released object to head of available objects list
   122	 */
   123	function Pool (factory) {
   124	  if (!(this instanceof Pool)) {
   125	    return new Pool(factory)
   126	  }
   127	
   128	  if (factory.validate && factory.validateAsync) {
   129	    throw new Error('Only one of validate or validateAsync may be specified')
   130	  }
   131	
   132	  // defaults
   133	  factory.idleTimeoutMillis = factory.idleTimeoutMillis || 30000
   134	  factory.returnToHead = factory.returnToHead || false
   135	  factory.refreshIdle = ('refreshIdle' in factory) ? factory.refreshIdle : true
   136	  factory.reapInterval = factory.reapIntervalMillis || 1000
   137	  factory.priorityRange = factory.priorityRange || 1
   138	  factory.validate = factory.validate || function () { return true }
   139	
   140	  factory.max = parseInt(factory.max, 10)
   141	  factory.min = parseInt(factory.min, 10)
   142	
   143	  factory.max = Math.max(isNaN(factory.max) ? 1 : factory.max, 1)
   144	  factory.min = Math.min(isNaN(factory.min) ? 0 : factory.min, factory.max - 1)
   145	
   146	  this._factory = factory
   147	  this._inUseObjects = []
   148	  this._draining = false
   149	  this._waitingClients = new PriorityQueue(factory.priorityRange)
   150	  this._availableObjects = []
   151	  this._count = 0
   152	  this._removeIdleTimer = null
   153	  this._removeIdleScheduled = false
   154	
   155	  // create initial resources (if factory.min > 0)
   156	  this._ensureMinimum()
   157	}
   158	
   159	/**
   160	 * logs to console or user defined log function
   161	 * @private
   162	 * @param {string} str
   163	 * @param {string} level
   164	 */
   165	Pool.prototype._log = function log (str, level) {
   166	  if (typeof this._factory.log === 'function') {
   167	    this._factory.log(str, level)
   168	  } else if (this._factory.log) {
   169	    console.log(level.toUpperCase() + ' pool ' + this._factory.name + ' - ' + str)
   170	  }
   171	}
   172	
   173	/**
   174	 * Request the client to be destroyed. The factory's destroy handler
   175	 * will also be called.
   176	 *
   177	 * This should be called within an acquire() block as an alternative to release().
   178	 *
   179	 * @param {Object} obj
   180	 *   The acquired item to be destoyed.
   181	 */
   182	Pool.prototype.destroy = function destroy (obj) {
   183	  this._count -= 1
   184	  if (this._count < 0) this._count = 0
   185	  this._availableObjects = this._availableObjects.filter(function (objWithTimeout) {
   186	    return (objWithTimeout.obj !== obj)
   187	  })
   188	
   189	  this._inUseObjects = this._inUseObjects.filter(function (objInUse) {
   190	    return (objInUse !== obj)
   191	  })
   192	
   193	  this._factory.destroy(obj)
   194	
   195	  this._ensureMinimum()
   196	}
   197	
   198	/**
   199	 * Checks and removes the available (idle) clients that have timed out.
   200	 * @private
   201	 */
   202	Pool.prototype._removeIdle = function removeIdle () {
   203	  var toRemove = []
   204	  var now = new Date().getTime()
   205	  var i
   206	  var al
   207	  var tr
   208	  var timeout
   209	
   210	  this._removeIdleScheduled = false
   211	
   212	  // Go through the available (idle) items,
   213	  // check if they have timed out
   214	  for (i = 0, al = this._availableObjects.length; i < al && (this._factory.refreshIdle && (this._count - this._factory.min > toRemove.length)); i += 1) {
   215	    timeout = this._availableObjects[i].timeout
   216	    if (now >= timeout) {
   217	      // Client timed out, so destroy it.
   218	      this._log('removeIdle() destroying obj - now:' + now + ' timeout:' + timeout, 'verbose')
   219	      toRemove.push(this._availableObjects[i].obj)
   220	    }
   221	  }
   222	
   223	  for (i = 0, tr = toRemove.length; i < tr; i += 1) {
   224	    this.destroy(toRemove[i])
   225	  }
   226	
   227	  // Replace the available items with the ones to keep.
   228	  al = this._availableObjects.length
   229	
   230	  if (al > 0) {
   231	    this._log('this._availableObjects.length=' + al, 'verbose')
   232	    this._scheduleRemoveIdle()
   233	  } else {
   234	    this._log('removeIdle() all objects removed', 'verbose')
   235	  }
   236	}
   237	
   238	/**
   239	 * Schedule removal of idle items in the pool.
   240	 *
   241	 * More schedules cannot run concurrently.
   242	 */
   243	Pool.prototype._scheduleRemoveIdle = function scheduleRemoveIdle () {
   244	  var self = this
   245	  if (!this._removeIdleScheduled) {
   246	    this._removeIdleScheduled = true
   247	    this._removeIdleTimer = setTimeout(function () {
   248	      self._removeIdle()
   249	    }, this._factory.reapInterval)
   250	  }
   251	}
   252	
   253	/**
   254	 * Try to get a new client to work, and clean up pool unused (idle) items.
   255	 *
   256	 *  - If there are available clients waiting, shift the first one out (LIFO),
   257	 *    and call its callback.
   258	 *  - If there are no waiting clients, try to create one if it won't exceed
   259	 *    the maximum number of clients.
   260	 *  - If creating a new client would exceed the maximum, add the client to
   261	 *    the wait list.
   262	 * @private
   263	 */
   264	Pool.prototype._dispense = function dispense () {
   265	  var self = this
   266	  var objWithTimeout = null
   267	  var err = null
   268	  var clientCb = null
   269	  var waitingCount = this._waitingClients.size()
   270	
   271	  this._log('dispense() clients=' + waitingCount + ' available=' + this._availableObjects.length, 'info')
   272	  if (waitingCount > 0) {
   273	    if (this._factory.validateAsync) {
   274	      doWhileAsync(function () {
   275	        return self._availableObjects.length > 0
   276	      }, function (next) {
   277	        self._log('dispense() - reusing obj', 'verbose')
   278	        objWithTimeout = self._availableObjects[0]
   279	
   280	        self._factory.validateAsync(objWithTimeout.obj, function (valid) {
   281	          if (!valid) {
   282	            self.destroy(objWithTimeout.obj)
   283	            next()
   284	          } else {
   285	            self._availableObjects.shift()
   286	            self._inUseObjects.push(objWithTimeout.obj)
   287	            clientCb = self._waitingClients.dequeue()
   288	            clientCb(err, objWithTimeout.obj)
   289	          }
   290	        })
   291	      }, function () {
   292	        if (self._count < self._factory.max) {
   293	          self._createResource()
   294	        }
   295	      })
   296	
   297	      return
   298	    }
   299	
   300	    while (this._availableObjects.length > 0) {
   301	      this._log('dispense() - reusing obj', 'verbose')
   302	      objWithTimeout = this._availableObjects[0]
   303	      if (!this._factory.validate(objWithTimeout.obj)) {
   304	        this.destroy(objWithTimeout.obj)
   305	        continue
   306	      }
   307	      this._availableObjects.shift()
   308	      this._inUseObjects.push(objWithTimeout.obj)
   309	      clientCb = this._waitingClients.dequeue()
   310	      return clientCb(err, objWithTimeout.obj)
   311	    }
   312	    if (this._count < this._factory.max) {
   313	      this._createResource()
   314	    }
   315	  }
   316	}
   317	
   318	/**
   319	 * @private
   320	 */
   321	Pool.prototype._createResource = function _createResource () {
   322	  this._count += 1
   323	  this._log('createResource() - creating obj - count=' + this._count + ' min=' + this._factory.min + ' max=' + this._factory.max, 'verbose')
   324	  var self = this
   325	  this._factory.create(function () {
   326	    var err, obj
   327	    var clientCb = self._waitingClients.dequeue()
   328	    if (arguments.length > 1) {
   329	      err = arguments[0]
   330	      obj = arguments[1]
   331	    } else {
   332	      err = (arguments[0] instanceof Error) ? arguments[0] : null
   333	      obj = (arguments[0] instanceof Error) ? null : arguments[0]
   334	    }
   335	    if (err) {
   336	      self._count -= 1
   337	      if (self._count < 0) self._count = 0
   338	      if (clientCb) {
   339	        clientCb(err, obj)
   340	      }
   341	      process.nextTick(function () {
   342	        self._dispense()
   343	      })
   344	    } else {
   345	      self._inUseObjects.push(obj)
   346	      if (clientCb) {
   347	        clientCb(err, obj)
   348	      } else {
   349	        self.release(obj)
   350	      }
   351	    }
   352	  })
   353	}
   354	
   355	/**
   356	 * @private
   357	 */
   358	Pool.prototype._ensureMinimum = function _ensureMinimum () {
   359	  var i, diff
   360	  if (!this._draining && (this._count < this._factory.min)) {
   361	    diff = this._factory.min - this._count
   362	    for (i = 0; i < diff; i++) {
   363	      this._createResource()
   364	    }
   365	  }
   366	}
   367	
   368	/**
   369	 * Request a new client. The callback will be called,
   370	 * when a new client will be availabe, passing the client to it.
   371	 *
   372	 * @param {Function} callback
   373	 *   Callback function to be called after the acquire is successful.
   374	 *   The function will receive the acquired item as the first parameter.
   375	 *
   376	 * @param {Number} priority
   377	 *   Optional.  Integer between 0 and (priorityRange - 1).  Specifies the priority
   378	 *   of the caller if there are no available resources.  Lower numbers mean higher
   379	 *   priority.
   380	 *
   381	 * @returns {boolean} `true` if the pool is not fully utilized, `false` otherwise.
   382	 */
   383	Pool.prototype.acquire = function acquire (callback, priority) {
   384	  if (this._draining) {
   385	    throw new Error('pool is draining and cannot accept work')
   386	  }
   387	  this._waitingClients.enqueue(callback, priority)
   388	  this._dispense()
   389	  return (this._count < this._factory.max)
   390	}
   391	
   392	/**
   393	 * @deprecated
   394	 */
   395	Pool.prototype.borrow = function borrow (callback, priority) {
   396	  this._log('borrow() is deprecated. use acquire() instead', 'warn')
   397	  this.acquire(callback, priority)
   398	}
   399	
   400	/**
   401	 * Return the client to the pool, in case it is no longer required.
   402	 *
   403	 * @param {Object} obj
   404	 *   The acquired object to be put back to the pool.
   405	 */
   406	Pool.prototype.release = function release (obj) {
   407	  // check to see if this object has already been released (i.e., is back in the pool of this._availableObjects)
   408	  if (this._availableObjects.some(function (objWithTimeout) { return (objWithTimeout.obj === obj) })) {
   409	    this._log('release called twice for the same resource: ' + (new Error().stack), 'error')
   410	    return
   411	  }
   412	
   413	  // check to see if this object exists in the `in use` list and remove it
   414	  var index = this._inUseObjects.indexOf(obj)
   415	  if (index < 0) {
   416	    this._log('attempt to release an invalid resource: ' + (new Error().stack), 'error')
   417	    return
   418	  }
   419	
   420	  // this._log("return to pool")
   421	  this._inUseObjects.splice(index, 1)
   422	  var objWithTimeout = { obj: obj, timeout: (new Date().getTime() + this._factory.idleTimeoutMillis) }
   423	  if (this._factory.returnToHead) {
   424	    this._availableObjects.splice(0, 0, objWithTimeout)
   425	  } else {
   426	    this._availableObjects.push(objWithTimeout)
   427	  }
   428	  this._log('timeout: ' + objWithTimeout.timeout, 'verbose')
   429	  this._dispense()
   430	  this._scheduleRemoveIdle()
   431	}
   432	
   433	/**
   434	 * @deprecated
   435	 */
   436	Pool.prototype.returnToPool = function returnToPool (obj) {
   437	  this._log('returnToPool() is deprecated. use release() instead', 'warn')
   438	  this.release(obj)
   439	}
   440	
   441	/**
   442	 * Disallow any new requests and let the request backlog dissapate.
   443	 *
   444	 * @param {Function} callback
   445	 *   Optional. Callback invoked when all work is done and all clients have been
   446	 *   released.
   447	 */
   448	Pool.prototype.drain = function drain (callback) {
   449	  this._log('draining', 'info')
   450	
   451	  // disable the ability to put more work on the queue.
   452	  this._draining = true
   453	
   454	  var self = this
   455	  var check = function () {
   456	    if (self._waitingClients.size() > 0) {
   457	      // wait until all client requests have been satisfied.
   458	      setTimeout(check, 100)
   459	    } else if (self._availableObjects.length !== self._count) {
   460	      // wait until all objects have been released.
   461	      setTimeout(check, 100)
   462	    } else if (callback) {
   463	      callback()
   464	    }
   465	  }
   466	  check()
   467	}
   468	
   469	/**
   470	 * Forcibly destroys all clients regardless of timeout.  Intended to be
   471	 * invoked as part of a drain.  Does not prevent the creation of new
   472	 * clients as a result of subsequent calls to acquire.
   473	 *
   474	 * Note that if factory.min > 0, the pool will destroy all idle resources
   475	 * in the pool, but replace them with newly created resources up to the
   476	 * specified factory.min value.  If this is not desired, set factory.min
   477	 * to zero before calling destroyAllNow()
   478	 *
   479	 * @param {Function} callback
   480	 *   Optional. Callback invoked after all existing clients are destroyed.
   481	 */
   482	Pool.prototype.destroyAllNow = function destroyAllNow (callback) {
   483	  this._log('force destroying all objects', 'info')
   484	  var willDie = this._availableObjects
   485	  this._availableObjects = []
   486	  var obj = willDie.shift()
   487	  while (obj !== null && obj !== undefined) {
   488	    this.destroy(obj.obj)
   489	    obj = willDie.shift()
   490	  }
   491	  this._removeIdleScheduled = false
   492	  clearTimeout(this._removeIdleTimer)
   493	  if (callback) {
   494	    callback()
   495	  }
   496	}
   497	
   498	/**
   499	 * Decorates a function to use a acquired client from the object pool when called.
   500	 *
   501	 * @param {Function} decorated
   502	 *   The decorated function, accepting a client as the first argument and
   503	 *   (optionally) a callback as the final argument.
   504	 *
   505	 * @param {Number} priority
   506	 *   Optional.  Integer between 0 and (priorityRange - 1).  Specifies the priority
   507	 *   of the caller if there are no available resources.  Lower numbers mean higher
   508	 *   priority.
   509	 */
   510	Pool.prototype.pooled = function pooled (decorated, priority) {
   511	  var self = this
   512	  return function () {
   513	    var callerArgs = arguments
   514	    var callerCallback = callerArgs[callerArgs.length - 1]
   515	    var callerHasCallback = typeof callerCallback === 'function'
   516	    self.acquire(function (err, client) {
   517	      if (err) {
   518	        if (callerHasCallback) {
   519	          callerCallback(err)
   520	        }
   521	        return
   522	      }
   523	
   524	      var args = [client].concat(Array.prototype.slice.call(callerArgs, 0, callerHasCallback ? -1 : undefined))
   525	      args.push(function () {
   526	        self.release(client)
   527	        if (callerHasCallback) {
   528	          callerCallback.apply(null, arguments)
   529	        }
   530	      })
   531	
   532	      decorated.apply(null, args)
   533	    }, priority)
   534	  }
   535	}
   536	
   537	Pool.prototype.getPoolSize = function getPoolSize () {
   538	  return this._count
   539	}
   540	
   541	Pool.prototype.getName = function getName () {
   542	  return this._factory.name
   543	}
   544	
   545	Pool.prototype.availableObjectsCount = function availableObjectsCount () {
   546	  return this._availableObjects.length
   547	}
   548	
   549	Pool.prototype.inUseObjectsCount = function inUseObjectsCount () {
   550	  return this._inUseObjects.length
   551	}
   552	
   553	Pool.prototype.waitingClientsCount = function waitingClientsCount () {
   554	  return this._waitingClients.size()
   555	}
   556	
   557	Pool.prototype.getMaxPoolSize = function getMaxPoolSize () {
   558	  return this._factory.max
   559	}
   560	
   561	Pool.prototype.getMinPoolSize = function getMinPoolSize () {
   562	  return this._factory.min
   563	}
   564	
   565	exports.Pool = Pool

     1	{
     2	  "name": "generic-pool",

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

     1	[![build status](https://secure.travis-ci.org/coopernurse/node-pool.png)](http://travis-ci.org/coopernurse/node-pool)
     2	
     3	# About
     4	
     5	  Generic resource pool.  Can be used to reuse or throttle expensive resources such as
     6	  database connections.
     7	
     8	## Installation
     9	
    10	    $ npm install generic-pool
    11	
    12	## History
    13	
    14	The history has been moved to the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)
    15	
    16	## Example
    17	
    18	### Step 1 - Create pool using a factory object
    19	
    20	```js
    21	// Create a MySQL connection pool with
    22	// a max of 10 connections, a min of 2, and a 30 second max idle time
    23	var Pool = require('generic-pool').Pool;
    24	var mysql = require('mysql'); // v2.10.x
    25	
    26	var pool = new Pool({
    27	    name     : 'mysql',
    28	    create   : function(callback) {
    29	        var c = mysql.createConnection({
    30	                user: 'scott',
    31	                password: 'tiger',
    32	                database:'mydb'
    33	        })
    34	
    35	        // parameter order: err, resource
    36	        callback(null, c);
    37	    },
    38	    destroy  : function(client) { client.end(); },
    39	    max      : 10,
    40	    // optional. if you set this, make sure to drain() (see step 3)
    41	    min      : 2,
    42	    // specifies how long a resource can stay idle in pool before being removed
    43	    idleTimeoutMillis : 30000,
    44	     // if true, logs via console.log - can also be a function
    45	    log : true
    46	});
    47	```
    48	
    49	### Step 2 - Use pool in your code to acquire/release resources
    50	
    51	```js
    52	// acquire connection - callback function is called
    53	// once a resource becomes available
    54	pool.acquire(function(err, client) {
    55	    if (err) {
    56	        // handle error - this is generally the err from your
    57	        // factory.create function
    58	    }
    59	    else {
    60	        client.query("select * from foo", [], function() {
    61	            // return object back to pool
    62	            pool.release(client);
    63	        });
    64	    }
    65	});
    66	```
    67	
    68	### Step 3 - Drain pool during shutdown (optional)
    69	
    70	If you are shutting down a long-lived process, you may notice
    71	that node fails to exit for 30 seconds or so.  This is a side
    72	effect of the idleTimeoutMillis behavior -- the pool has a
    73	setTimeout() call registered that is in the event loop queue, so
    74	node won't terminate until all resources have timed out, and the pool
    75	stops trying to manage them.
    76	
    77	This behavior will be more problematic when you set factory.min > 0,
    78	as the pool will never become empty, and the setTimeout calls will
    79	never end.
    80	
    81	In these cases, use the pool.drain() function.  This sets the pool
    82	into a "draining" state which will gracefully wait until all
    83	idle resources have timed out.  For example, you can call:
    84	
    85	```js
    86	// Only call this once in your application -- at the point you want
    87	// to shutdown and stop using this pool.
    88	pool.drain(function() {
    89	    pool.destroyAllNow();
    90	});
    91	```
    92	
    93	If you do this, your node process will exit gracefully.
    94	
    95	
    96	## Documentation
    97	
    98	    Pool() accepts an object with these slots:
    99	
   100	                  name : name of pool (string, optional)
   101	                create : function that returns a new resource
   102	                           should call callback() with the created resource
   103	               destroy : function that accepts a resource and destroys it
   104	                   max : maximum number of resources to create at any given time
   105	                         optional (default=1)
   106	                   min : minimum number of resources to keep in pool at any given time
   107	                         if this is set >= max, the pool will silently set the min
   108	                         to factory.max - 1 (Note: min==max case is expected to change in v3 release)
   109	                         optional (default=0)
   110	           refreshIdle : boolean that specifies whether idle resources at or below the min threshold
   111	                         should be destroyed/re-created.  optional (default=true)
   112	     idleTimeoutMillis : max milliseconds a resource can go unused before it should be destroyed
   113	                         (default 30000)
   114	    reapIntervalMillis : frequency to check for idle resources (default 1000),
   115	          returnToHead : boolean, if true the most recently released resources will be the first to be allocated.
   116	                         This in effect turns the pool's behaviour from a queue into a stack. optional (default false)
   117	         priorityRange : int between 1 and x - if set, borrowers can specify their
   118	                         relative priority in the queue if no resources are available.
   119	                         see example.  (default 1)
   120	              validate : function that accepts a pooled resource and returns true if the resource
   121	                         is OK to use, or false if the object is invalid.  Invalid objects will be destroyed.
   122	                         This function is called in acquire() before returning a resource from the pool.
   123	                         Optional.  Default function always returns true.
   124	         validateAsync : Asynchronous validate function. Receives a callback function as its second argument,
   125	                         which should be called with a single boolean argument being true if the item is still
   126	                         valid and false if it should be removed from the pool. Called before item is acquired
   127	                         from pool. Default is undefined. Only one of validate/validateAsync may be specified
   128	                   log : true/false or function -
   129	                           If a log is a function, it will be called with two parameters:
   130	                                                    - log string
   131	                                                    - log level ('verbose', 'info', 'warn', 'error')
   132	                           Else if log is true, verbose log info will be sent to console.log()
   133	                           Else internal log messages be ignored (this is the default)
   134	
   135	## Priority Queueing
   136	
   137	The pool now supports optional priority queueing.  This becomes relevant when no resources
   138	are available and the caller has to wait. `acquire()` accepts an optional priority int which
   139	specifies the caller's relative position in the queue.
   140	
   141	```js
   142	 // create pool with priorityRange of 3
   143	 // borrowers can specify a priority 0 to 2
   144	 var pool = new Pool({
   145	     name     : 'mysql',
   146	     create   : function(callback) {
   147	         // do something
   148	     },
   149	     destroy  : function(client) {
   150	         // cleanup.  omitted for this example
   151	     },
   152	     max      : 10,
   153	     idleTimeoutMillis : 30000,
   154	     priorityRange : 3
   155	 });
   156	
   157	 // acquire connection - no priority - will go at front of line (same as high priority)
   158	 pool.acquire(function(err, client) {
   159	     pool.release(client);
   160	 });
   161	
   162	 // acquire connection - high priority - will go into front slot
   163	 pool.acquire(function(err, client) {
   164	     pool.release(client);
   165	 }, 0);
   166	
   167	 // acquire connection - medium priority - will go into middle slot
   168	 pool.acquire(function(err, client) {
   169	     pool.release(client);
   170	 }, 1);
   171	
   172	 // etc..
   173	```
   174	
   175	## Draining
   176	
   177	If you know would like to terminate all the resources in your pool before
   178	their timeouts have been reached, you can use `destroyAllNow()` in conjunction
   179	with `drain()`:
   180	
   181	```js
   182	pool.drain(function() {
   183	    pool.destroyAllNow();
   184	});
   185	```
   186	
   187	One side-effect of calling `drain()` is that subsequent calls to `acquire()`
   188	will throw an Error.
   189	
   190	## Pooled function decoration
   191	
   192	To transparently handle object acquisition for a function,
   193	one can use `pooled()`:
   194	
   195	```js
   196	var privateFn, publicFn;
   197	publicFn = pool.pooled(privateFn = function(client, arg, cb) {
   198	    // Do something with the client and arg. Client is auto-released when cb is called
   199	    cb(null, arg);
   200	});
   201	```
   202	
   203	Keeping both private and public versions of each function allows for pooled
   204	functions to call other pooled functions with the same member. This is a handy
   205	pattern for database transactions:
   206	
   207	```js
   208	var privateTop, privateBottom, publicTop, publicBottom;
   209	publicBottom = pool.pooled(privateBottom = function(client, arg, cb) {
   210	    //Use client, assumed auto-release
   211	});
   212	
   213	publicTop = pool.pooled(privateTop = function(client, cb) {
   214	    // e.g., open a database transaction
   215	    privateBottom(client, "arg", function(err, retVal) {
   216	        if(err) { return cb(err); }
   217	        // e.g., close a transaction
   218	        cb();
   219	    });
   220	});
   221	```
   222	
   223	## Pool info
   224	
   225	The following functions will let you get information about the pool:
   226	
   227	```js
   228	// returns factory.name for this pool
   229	pool.getName()
   230	
   231	// returns number of resources in the pool regardless of
   232	// whether they are free or in use
   233	pool.getPoolSize()
   234	
   235	// returns number of unused resources in the pool
   236	pool.availableObjectsCount()
   237	
   238	// returns number of callers waiting to acquire a resource
   239	pool.waitingClientsCount()
   240	
   241	// returns number of maxixmum number of resources allowed by ppol
   242	pool.getMaxPoolSize()
   243	
   244	// returns number of minimum number of resources allowed by ppol
   245	pool.getMinPoolSize()
   246	
   247	```
   248	
   249	## Run Tests
   250	
   251	    $ npm install expresso
   252	    $ npm test
   253	
   254	The test runner runs every test in parallel, so tests cannot safely share
   255	resources. If a test fails, its thrown assertion error may bubble up and halt
   256	execution/cause failures in other running tests; these are spurious. If you
   257	have a failing test, try running it in isolation until you get it to pass.
   258	
   259	The individual tests "wait" by repeatedly checking the condition in the
   260	`beforeExit` callback. The test is marked as "passed" if the `beforeExit`
   261	callback runs successfully. Generally, this is accomplished by counting the
   262	number of assertions and checking that all of the test's assertions have been
   263	asserted.

   204	    var created = 0
   205	    var destroyed = 0
   206	    var count = 5
   207	    var acquired = 0
   208	
   209	    var pool = poolModule.Pool({
   210	      name: 'test4',
   211	      create: function (callback) { callback(null, {id: ++created}) },
   212	      destroy: function (client) { destroyed += 1 },
   213	      max: 2,
   214	      idletimeoutMillis: 300000
   215	    })
   216	
   217	    for (var i = 0; i < count; i++) {
   218	      pool.acquire(function (err, client) {
   219	        assert.ifError(err)
   220	        acquired += 1
   221	        assert.equal(typeof client.id, 'number')
   222	        setTimeout(function () { pool.release(client) }, 250)
   223	      })
   224	    }
   225	
   226	    assert.notEqual(count, acquired)
   227	    pool.drain(function () {
   228	      assert.equal(count, acquired)
   229	      // short circuit the absurdly long timeouts above.
   230	      pool.destroyAllNow()
   231	      beforeExit(function () {})
   232	    })
   233	
   234	    // subsequent calls to acquire should return an error.
   235	    assert.throws(function () {
   236	      pool.acquire(function (client) {})
   237	    }, Error)
   238	  },

   540	      assert.equal(logmessages.info[0], 'dispense() clients=1 available=0')
   541	      logmessages.info = []

   251	/* adapted from https://github.com/lodash/lodash/blob/4.17.15/dist/lodash.js#L6735-L6744 */
   252	var rePropName = /[^%.[\]]+|\[(?:(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)|(["'])((?:(?!\2)[^\\]|\\.)*?)\2)\]|(?=(?:\.|\[\])(?:\.|\[\]|%$))/g;
   253	var reEscapeChar = /\\(\\)?/g; /** Used to match backslashes in property paths. */
   254	var stringToPath = function stringToPath(string) {
   255		var first = $strSlice(string, 0, 1);
   256		var last = $strSlice(string, -1);
   257		if (first === '%' && last !== '%') {
   258			throw new $SyntaxError('invalid intrinsic syntax, expected closing `%`');
   259		} else if (last === '%' && first !== '%') {
   260			throw new $SyntaxError('invalid intrinsic syntax, expected opening `%`');
   261		}
   262		var result = [];
   263		$replace(string, rePropName, function (match, number, quote, subString) {
   264			result[result.length] = quote ? $replace(subString, reEscapeChar, '$1') : number || match;
   265		});
   266		return result;
   267	};

   270	var getBaseIntrinsic = function getBaseIntrinsic(name, allowMissing) {
   271		var intrinsicName = name;
   272		var alias;
   273		if (hasOwn(LEGACY_ALIASES, intrinsicName)) {
   274			alias = LEGACY_ALIASES[intrinsicName];
   275			intrinsicName = '%' + alias[0] + '%';
   276		}
   277	
   278		if (hasOwn(INTRINSICS, intrinsicName)) {
   279			var value = INTRINSICS[intrinsicName];
   280			if (value === needsEval) {
   281				value = doEval(intrinsicName);
   282			}
   283			if (typeof value === 'undefined' && !allowMissing) {
   284				throw new $TypeError('intrinsic ' + name + ' exists, but is not available. Please file an issue!');
   285			}
   286	
   287			return {
   288				alias: alias,
   289				name: intrinsicName,
   290				value: value
   291			};
   292		}
   293	
   294		throw new $SyntaxError('intrinsic ' + name + ' does not exist!');
   295	};

   297	module.exports = function GetIntrinsic(name, allowMissing) {
   298		if (typeof name !== 'string' || name.length === 0) {
   299			throw new $TypeError('intrinsic name must be a non-empty string');
   300		}
   301		if (arguments.length > 1 && typeof allowMissing !== 'boolean') {
   302			throw new $TypeError('"allowMissing" argument must be a boolean');
   303		}
   304	
   305		if ($exec(/^%?[^%]*%?$/, name) === null) {
   306			throw new $SyntaxError('`%` may not be present anywhere but at the beginning and end of the intrinsic name');
   307		}
   308		var parts = stringToPath(name);
   309		var intrinsicBaseName = parts.length > 0 ? parts[0] : '';
   310	
   311		var intrinsic = getBaseIntrinsic('%' + intrinsicBaseName + '%', allowMissing);
   312		var intrinsicRealName = intrinsic.name;
   313		var value = intrinsic.value;
   314		var skipFurtherCaching = false;
   315	
   316		var alias = intrinsic.alias;
   317		if (alias) {
   318			intrinsicBaseName = alias[0];
   319			$spliceApply(parts, $concat([0, 1], alias));
   320		}
   321	
   322		for (var i = 1, isOwn = true; i < parts.length; i += 1) {
   323			var part = parts[i];
   324			var first = $strSlice(part, 0, 1);
   325			var last = $strSlice(part, -1);
   326			if (
   327				(
   328					(first === '"' || first === "'" || first === '`')
   329					|| (last === '"' || last === "'" || last === '`')
   330				)
   331				&& first !== last
   332			) {
   333				throw new $SyntaxError('property names with quotes must have matching quotes');
   334			}
   335			if (part === 'constructor' || !isOwn) {
   336				skipFurtherCaching = true;
   337			}
   338	
   339			intrinsicBaseName += '.' + part;
   340			intrinsicRealName = '%' + intrinsicBaseName + '%';
   341	
   342			if (hasOwn(INTRINSICS, intrinsicRealName)) {
   343				value = INTRINSICS[intrinsicRealName];
   344			} else if (value != null) {
   345				if (!(part in value)) {
   346					if (!allowMissing) {
   347						throw new $TypeError('base intrinsic for ' + name + ' exists, but the property is not available.');
   348					}
   349					return void undefined;
   350				}
   351				if ($gOPD && (i + 1) >= parts.length) {
   352					var desc = $gOPD(value, part);
   353					isOwn = !!desc;
   354	
   355					// By convention, when a data property is converted to an accessor
   356					// property to emulate a data property that does not suffer from
   357					// the override mistake, that accessor's getter is marked with
   358					// an `originalValue` property. Here, when we detect this, we
   359					// uphold the illusion by pretending to see that original data
   360					// property, i.e., returning the value rather than the getter
   361					// itself.
   362					if (isOwn && 'get' in desc && !('originalValue' in desc.get)) {
   363						value = desc.get;
   364					} else {
   365						value = value[part];
   366					}
   367				} else {
   368					isOwn = hasOwn(value, part);
   369					value = value[part];
   370				}
   371	
   372				if (isOwn && !skipFurtherCaching) {
   373					INTRINSICS[intrinsicRealName] = value;
   374				}
   375			}
   376		}
   377		return value;
   378	};

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

     1	# get-intrinsic <sup>[![Version Badge][npm-version-svg]][package-url]</sup>
     2	
     3	[![github actions][actions-image]][actions-url]
     4	[![coverage][codecov-image]][codecov-url]
     5	[![dependency status][deps-svg]][deps-url]
     6	[![dev dependency status][dev-deps-svg]][dev-deps-url]
     7	[![License][license-image]][license-url]
     8	[![Downloads][downloads-image]][downloads-url]
     9	
    10	[![npm badge][npm-badge-png]][package-url]
    11	
    12	Get and robustly cache all JS language-level intrinsics at first require time.
    13	
    14	See the syntax described [in the JS spec](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-well-known-intrinsic-objects) for reference.
    15	
    16	## Example
    17	
    18	```js
    19	var GetIntrinsic = require('get-intrinsic');
    20	var assert = require('assert');
    21	
    22	// static methods
    23	assert.equal(GetIntrinsic('%Math.pow%'), Math.pow);
    24	assert.equal(Math.pow(2, 3), 8);
    25	assert.equal(GetIntrinsic('%Math.pow%')(2, 3), 8);
    26	delete Math.pow;
    27	assert.equal(GetIntrinsic('%Math.pow%')(2, 3), 8);
    28	
    29	// instance methods
    30	var arr = [1];
    31	assert.equal(GetIntrinsic('%Array.prototype.push%'), Array.prototype.push);
    32	assert.deepEqual(arr, [1]);
    33	
    34	arr.push(2);
    35	assert.deepEqual(arr, [1, 2]);
    36	
    37	GetIntrinsic('%Array.prototype.push%').call(arr, 3);
    38	assert.deepEqual(arr, [1, 2, 3]);
    39	
    40	delete Array.prototype.push;
    41	GetIntrinsic('%Array.prototype.push%').call(arr, 4);
    42	assert.deepEqual(arr, [1, 2, 3, 4]);
    43	
    44	// missing features
    45	delete JSON.parse; // to simulate a real intrinsic that is missing in the environment
    46	assert.throws(() => GetIntrinsic('%JSON.parse%'));
    47	assert.equal(undefined, GetIntrinsic('%JSON.parse%', true));
    48	```
    49	
    50	## Tests
    51	Simply clone the repo, `npm install`, and run `npm test`
    52	
    53	## Security
    54	
    55	Please email [@ljharb](https://github.com/ljharb) or see https://tidelift.com/security if you have a potential security vulnerability to report.

   129			var original = GetIntrinsic('%ObjProto_toString%');

   131			forEach([
   132				'%Object.prototype.toString%',

     1	# get-proto <sup>[![Version Badge][npm-version-svg]][package-url]</sup>
     2	
     3	[![github actions][actions-image]][actions-url]
     4	[![coverage][codecov-image]][codecov-url]
     5	[![License][license-image]][license-url]
     6	[![Downloads][downloads-image]][downloads-url]
     7	
     8	[![npm badge][npm-badge-png]][package-url]
     9	
    10	Robustly get the [[Prototype]] of an object. Uses the best available method.
    11	
    12	## Getting started
    13	
    14	```sh
    15	npm install --save get-proto
    16	```
    17	
    18	## Usage/Examples
    19	
    20	```js
    21	const assert = require('assert');
    22	const getProto = require('get-proto');
    23	
    24	const a = { a: 1, b: 2, [Symbol.toStringTag]: 'foo' };
    25	const b = { c: 3, __proto__: a };
    26	
    27	assert.equal(getProto(b), a);
    28	assert.equal(getProto(a), Object.prototype);
    29	assert.equal(getProto({ __proto__: null }), null);
    30	```
    31	
    32	## Tests
    33	
    34	Clone the repo, `npm install`, and run `npm test`

     1	'use strict';
     2	
     3	var test = require('tape');
     4	
     5	var getProto = require('../');
     6	
     7	test('getProto', function (t) {
     8		t.equal(typeof getProto, 'function', 'is a function');
     9	
    10		t.test('can get', { skip: !getProto }, function (st) {
    11			if (getProto) { // TS doesn't understand tape's skip
    12				var proto = { b: 2 };
    13				st.equal(getProto(proto), Object.prototype, 'proto: returns the [[Prototype]]');
    14	
    15				st.test('nullish value', function (s2t) {
    16				// @ts-expect-error
    17					s2t['throws'](function () { return getProto(undefined); }, TypeError, 'undefined is not an object');
    18					// @ts-expect-error
    19					s2t['throws'](function () { return getProto(null); }, TypeError, 'null is not an object');
    20					s2t.end();
    21				});
    22	
    23				// @ts-expect-error
    24				st['throws'](function () { getProto(true); }, 'throws for true');
    25				// @ts-expect-error
    26				st['throws'](function () { getProto(false); }, 'throws for false');
    27				// @ts-expect-error
    28				st['throws'](function () { getProto(42); }, 'throws for 42');
    29				// @ts-expect-error
    30				st['throws'](function () { getProto(NaN); }, 'throws for NaN');
    31				// @ts-expect-error
    32				st['throws'](function () { getProto(0); }, 'throws for +0');
    33				// @ts-expect-error
    34				st['throws'](function () { getProto(-0); }, 'throws for -0');
    35				// @ts-expect-error
    36				st['throws'](function () { getProto(Infinity); }, 'throws for ∞');
    37				// @ts-expect-error
    38				st['throws'](function () { getProto(-Infinity); }, 'throws for -∞');
    39				// @ts-expect-error
    40				st['throws'](function () { getProto(''); }, 'throws for empty string');
    41				// @ts-expect-error
    42				st['throws'](function () { getProto('foo'); }, 'throws for non-empty string');
    43				st.equal(getProto(/a/g), RegExp.prototype);
    44				st.equal(getProto(new Date()), Date.prototype);
    45				st.equal(getProto(function () {}), Function.prototype);
    46				st.equal(getProto([]), Array.prototype);
    47				st.equal(getProto({}), Object.prototype);
    48	
    49				var nullObject = { __proto__: null };
    50				if ('toString' in nullObject) {
    51					st.comment('no null objects in this engine');
    52					st.equal(getProto(nullObject), Object.prototype, '"null" object has Object.prototype as [[Prototype]]');
    53				} else {
    54					st.equal(getProto(nullObject), null, 'null object has null [[Prototype]]');
    55				}
    56			}
    57	
    58			st.end();
    59		});
    60	
    61		t.test('can not get', { skip: !!getProto }, function (st) {
    62			st.equal(getProto, null);
    63	
    64			st.end();
    65		});
    66	
    67		t.end();
    68	});

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

     1	'use strict';
     2	
     3	var isGlob = require('is-glob');
     4	var pathPosixDirname = require('path').posix.dirname;
     5	var isWin32 = require('os').platform() === 'win32';
     6	
     7	var slash = '/';
     8	var backslash = /\\/g;
     9	var enclosure = /[\{\[].*[\}\]]$/;
    10	var globby = /(^|[^\\])([\{\[]|\([^\)]+$)/;
    11	var escaped = /\\([\!\*\?\|\[\]\(\)\{\}])/g;
    12	
    13	/**
    14	 * @param {string} str
    15	 * @param {Object} opts
    16	 * @param {boolean} [opts.flipBackslashes=true]
    17	 * @returns {string}
    18	 */
    19	module.exports = function globParent(str, opts) {
    20	  var options = Object.assign({ flipBackslashes: true }, opts);
    21	
    22	  // flip windows path separators
    23	  if (options.flipBackslashes && isWin32 && str.indexOf(slash) < 0) {
    24	    str = str.replace(backslash, slash);
    25	  }
    26	
    27	  // special case for strings ending in enclosure containing path separator
    28	  if (enclosure.test(str)) {
    29	    str += slash;
    30	  }
    31	
    32	  // preserves full path in case of trailing path separator
    33	  str += 'a';
    34	
    35	  // remove path parts that are globby
    36	  do {
    37	    str = pathPosixDirname(str);
    38	  } while (isGlob(str) || globby.test(str));
    39	
    40	  // remove escape chars and return result
    41	  return str.replace(escaped, '$1');
    42	};

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

     1	<p align="center">
     2	  <a href="https://gulpjs.com">
     3	    <img height="257" width="114" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gulpjs/artwork/master/gulp-2x.png">
     4	  </a>
     5	</p>
     6	
     7	# glob-parent
     8	
     9	[![NPM version][npm-image]][npm-url] [![Downloads][downloads-image]][npm-url] [![Azure Pipelines Build Status][azure-pipelines-image]][azure-pipelines-url] [![Travis Build Status][travis-image]][travis-url] [![AppVeyor Build Status][appveyor-image]][appveyor-url] [![Coveralls Status][coveralls-image]][coveralls-url] [![Gitter chat][gitter-image]][gitter-url]
    10	
    11	Extract the non-magic parent path from a glob string.
    12	
    13	## Usage
    14	
    15	```js
    16	var globParent = require('glob-parent');
    17	
    18	globParent('path/to/*.js'); // 'path/to'
    19	globParent('/root/path/to/*.js'); // '/root/path/to'
    20	globParent('/*.js'); // '/'
    21	globParent('*.js'); // '.'
    22	globParent('**/*.js'); // '.'
    23	globParent('path/{to,from}'); // 'path'
    24	globParent('path/!(to|from)'); // 'path'
    25	globParent('path/?(to|from)'); // 'path'
    26	globParent('path/+(to|from)'); // 'path'
    27	globParent('path/*(to|from)'); // 'path'
    28	globParent('path/@(to|from)'); // 'path'
    29	globParent('path/**/*'); // 'path'
    30	
    31	// if provided a non-glob path, returns the nearest dir
    32	globParent('path/foo/bar.js'); // 'path/foo'
    33	globParent('path/foo/'); // 'path/foo'
    34	globParent('path/foo'); // 'path' (see issue #3 for details)
    35	```
    36	
    37	## API
    38	
    39	### `globParent(maybeGlobString, [options])`
    40	
    41	Takes a string and returns the part of the path before the glob begins. Be aware of Escaping rules and Limitations below.
    42	
    43	#### options
    44	
    45	```js
    46	{
    47	  // Disables the automatic conversion of slashes for Windows
    48	  flipBackslashes: true
    49	}
    50	```
    51	
    52	## Escaping
    53	
    54	The following characters have special significance in glob patterns and must be escaped if you want them to be treated as regular path characters:
    55	
    56	- `?` (question mark) unless used as a path segment alone
    57	- `*` (asterisk)
    58	- `|` (pipe)
    59	- `(` (opening parenthesis)
    60	- `)` (closing parenthesis)
    61	- `{` (opening curly brace)
    62	- `}` (closing curly brace)
    63	- `[` (opening bracket)
    64	- `]` (closing bracket)
    65	
    66	**Example**
    67	
    68	```js
    69	globParent('foo/[bar]/') // 'foo'
    70	globParent('foo/\\[bar]/') // 'foo/[bar]'
    71	```
    72	
    73	## Limitations
    74	
    75	### Braces & Brackets
    76	This library attempts a quick and imperfect method of determining which path
    77	parts have glob magic without fully parsing/lexing the pattern. There are some
    78	advanced use cases that can trip it up, such as nested braces where the outer
    79	pair is escaped and the inner one contains a path separator. If you find
    80	yourself in the unlikely circumstance of being affected by this or need to
    81	ensure higher-fidelity glob handling in your library, it is recommended that you
    82	pre-process your input with [expand-braces] and/or [expand-brackets].
    83	
    84	### Windows
    85	Backslashes are not valid path separators for globs. If a path with backslashes
    86	is provided anyway, for simple cases, glob-parent will replace the path
    87	separator for you and return the non-glob parent path (now with
    88	forward-slashes, which are still valid as Windows path separators).
    89	
    90	This cannot be used in conjunction with escape characters.
    91	
    92	```js
    93	// BAD
    94	globParent('C:\\Program Files \\(x86\\)\\*.ext') // 'C:/Program Files /(x86/)'
    95	
    96	// GOOD
    97	globParent('C:/Program Files\\(x86\\)/*.ext') // 'C:/Program Files (x86)'
    98	```
    99	
   100	If you are using escape characters for a pattern without path parts (i.e.
   101	relative to `cwd`), prefix with `./` to avoid confusing glob-parent.
   102	
   103	```js
   104	// BAD
   105	globParent('foo \\[bar]') // 'foo '
   106	globParent('foo \\[bar]*') // 'foo '
   107	
   108	// GOOD
   109	globParent('./foo \\[bar]') // 'foo [bar]'
   110	globParent('./foo \\[bar]*') // '.'
   111	```
   112

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

     1	'use strict';
     2	module.exports = (flag, argv) => {
     3		argv = argv || process.argv;
     4		const prefix = flag.startsWith('-') ? '' : (flag.length === 1 ? '-' : '--');
     5		const pos = argv.indexOf(prefix + flag);
     6		const terminatorPos = argv.indexOf('--');
     7		return pos !== -1 && (terminatorPos === -1 ? true : pos < terminatorPos);
     8	};

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CONTENU :
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

     1	# has-flag [![Build Status](https://travis-ci.org/sindresorhus/has-flag.svg?branch=master)](https://travis-ci.org/sindresorhus/has-flag)
     2	
     3	> Check if [`argv`](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/process.html#process_process_argv) has a specific flag
     4	
     5	Correctly stops looking after an `--` argument terminator.
     6	
     7	
     8	## Install
     9	
    10	```
    11	$ npm install has-flag
    12	```
    13	
    14	
    15	## Usage
    16	
    17	```js
    18	// foo.js
    19	const hasFlag = require('has-flag');
    20	
    21	hasFlag('unicorn');
    22	//=> true
    23	
    24	hasFlag('--unicorn');
    25	//=> true
    26	
    27	hasFlag('f');
    28	//=> true
    29	
    30	hasFlag('-f');
    31	//=> true
    32	
    33	hasFlag('foo=bar');
    34	//=> true
    35	
    36	hasFlag('foo');
    37	//=> false
    38	
    39	hasFlag('rainbow');
    40	//=> false
    41	```
    42	
    43	```
    44	$ node foo.js -f --unicorn --foo=bar -- --rainbow
    45	```
    46	
    47	
    48	## API
    49	
    50	### hasFlag(flag, [argv])
    51	
    52	Returns a boolean for whether the flag exists.
    53	
    54	#### flag
    55	
    56	Type: `string`
    57	
    58	CLI flag to look for. The `--` prefix is optional.
    59	
    60	#### argv
    61	
    62	Type: `string[]`<br>
    63	Default: `process.argv`
    64	
    65	CLI arguments.
    66	
    67	
    68	## License
    69	
    70	MIT © [Sindre Sorhus](https://sindresorhus.com)

     1	# hasown <sup>[![Version Badge][npm-version-svg]][package-url]</sup>
     2	
     3	[![github actions][actions-image]][actions-url]
     4	[![coverage][codecov-image]][codecov-url]
     5	[![License][license-image]][license-url]
     6	[![Downloads][downloads-image]][downloads-url]
     7	
     8	[![npm badge][npm-badge-png]][package-url]
     9	
    10	A robust, ES3 compatible, "has own property" predicate.
    11	
    12	## Example
    13	
    14	```js
    15	const assert = require('assert');
    16	const hasOwn = require('hasown');
    17	
    18	assert.equal(hasOwn({}, 'toString'), false);
    19	assert.equal(hasOwn([], 'length'), true);
    20	assert.equal(hasOwn({ a: 42 }, 'a'), true);
    21	```
    22	
    23	## Tests
    24	Simply clone the repo, `npm install`, and run `npm test`

     1	'use strict';
     2	
     3	var origSymbol = typeof Symbol !== 'undefined' && Symbol;
     4	var hasSymbolSham = require('./shams');
     5	
     6	/** @type {import('.')} */
     7	module.exports = function hasNativeSymbols() {
     8		if (typeof origSymbol !== 'function') { return false; }
     9		if (typeof Symbol !== 'function') { return false; }
    10		if (typeof origSymbol('foo') !== 'symbol') { return false; }
    11		if (typeof Symbol('bar') !== 'symbol') { return false; }
    12	
    13		return hasSymbolSham();
    14	};

     1	# has-symbols <sup>[![Version Badge][2]][1]</sup>
     2	
     3	[![github actions][actions-image]][actions-url]
     4	[![coverage][codecov-image]][codecov-url]
     5	[![dependency status][5]][6]
     6	[![dev dependency status][7]][8]
     7	[![License][license-image]][license-url]
     8	[![Downloads][downloads-image]][downloads-url]
     9	
    10	[![npm badge][11]][1]
    11	
    12	Determine if the JS environment has Symbol support. Supports spec, or shams.
    13	
    14	## Example
    15	
    16	```js
    17	var hasSymbols = require('has-symbols');
    18	
    19	hasSymbols() === true; // if the environment has native Symbol support. Not polyfillable, not forgeable.
    20	
    21	var hasSymbolsKinda = require('has-symbols/shams');
    22	hasSymbolsKinda() === true; // if the environment has a Symbol sham that mostly follows the spec.
    23	```
    24	
    25	## Supported Symbol shams
    26	 - get-own-property-symbols [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/get-own-property-symbols) | [github](https://github.com/WebReflection/get-own-property-symbols)
    27	 - core-js [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/core-js) | [github](https://github.com/zloirock/core-js)
    28	
    29	## Tests
    30	Simply clone the repo, `npm install`, and run `npm test`

     1	'use strict';
     2	
     3	/** @type {import('./shams')} */
     4	/* eslint complexity: [2, 18], max-statements: [2, 33] */
     5	module.exports = function hasSymbols() {
     6		if (typeof Symbol !== 'function' || typeof Object.getOwnPropertySymbols !== 'function') { return false; }
     7		if (typeof Symbol.iterator === 'symbol') { return true; }
     8	
     9		/** @type {{ [k in symbol]?: unknown }} */
    10		var obj = {};
    11		var sym = Symbol('test');
    12		var symObj = Object(sym);
    13		if (typeof sym === 'string') { return false; }
    14	
    15		if (Object.prototype.toString.call(sym) !== '[object Symbol]') { return false; }
    16		if (Object.prototype.toString.call(symObj) !== '[object Symbol]') { return false; }
    17	
    18		// temp disabled per https://github.com/ljharb/object.assign/issues/17
    19		// if (sym instanceof Symbol) { return false; }
    20		// temp disabled per https://github.com/WebReflection/get-own-property-symbols/issues/4
    21		// if (!(symObj instanceof Symbol)) { return false; }
    22	
    23		// if (typeof Symbol.prototype.toString !== 'function') { return false; }
    24		// if (String(sym) !== Symbol.prototype.toString.call(sym)) { return false; }
    25	
    26		var symVal = 42;
    27		obj[sym] = symVal;
    28		for (var _ in obj) { return false; } // eslint-disable-line no-restricted-syntax, no-unreachable-loop
    29		if (typeof Object.keys === 'function' && Object.keys(obj).length !== 0) { return false; }
    30	
    31		if (typeof Object.getOwnPropertyNames === 'function' && Object.getOwnPropertyNames(obj).length !== 0) { return false; }
    32	
    33		var syms = Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(obj);
    34		if (syms.length !== 1 || syms[0] !== sym) { return false; }
    35	
    36		if (!Object.prototype.propertyIsEnumerable.call(obj, sym)) { return false; }
    37	
    38		if (typeof Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor === 'function') {
    39			// eslint-disable-next-line no-extra-parens
    40			var descriptor = /** @type {PropertyDescriptor} */ (Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(obj, sym));
    41			if (descriptor.value !== symVal || descriptor.enumerable !== true) { return false; }
    42		}
    43	
    44		return true;
    45	};

    27	module.exports.HttpError = createHttpErrorConstructor()
    28	module.exports.isHttpError = createIsHttpErrorFunction(module.exports.HttpError)

    31	populateConstructorExports(module.exports, statuses.codes, module.exports.HttpError)

    33	/**
    34	 * Get the code class of a status code.
    35	 * @private
    36	 */
    37	
    38	function codeClass (status) {
    39	  return Number(String(status).charAt(0) + '00')
    40	}
    41	
    42	/**
    43	 * Create a new HTTP Error.
    44	 *
    45	 * @returns {Error}
    46	 * @public
    47	 */
    48	
    49	function createError () {
    50	  // so much arity going on ~_~
    51	  var err
    52	  var msg
    53	  var status = 500
    54	  var props = {}
    55	  for (var i = 0; i < arguments.length; i++) {
    56	    var arg = arguments[i]
    57	    var type = typeof arg
    58	    if (type === 'object' && arg instanceof Error) {
    59	      err = arg
    60	      status = err.status || err.statusCode || status
    61	    } else if (type === 'number' && i === 0) {
    62	      status = arg
    63	    } else if (type === 'string') {
    64	      msg = arg
    65	    } else if (type === 'object') {
    66	      props = arg
    67	    } else {
    68	      throw new TypeError('argument #' + (i + 1) + ' unsupported type ' + type)
    69	    }
    70	  }
    71	
    72	  if (typeof status === 'number' && (status < 400 || status >= 600)) {
    73	    deprecate('non-error status code; use only 4xx or 5xx status codes')
    74	  }
    75	
    76	  if (typeof status !== 'number' ||
    77	    (!statuses.message[status] && (status < 400 || status >= 600))) {
    78	    status = 500
    79	  }
    80	
    81	  // constructor
    82	  var HttpError = createError[status] || createError[codeClass(status)]
    83	
    84	  if (!err) {
    85	    // create error
    86	    err = HttpError
    87	      ? new HttpError(msg)
    88	      : new Error(msg || statuses.message[status])
    89	    Error.captureStackTrace(err, createError)
    90	  }
    91	
    92	  if (!HttpError || !(err instanceof HttpError) || err.status !== status) {
    93	    // add properties to generic error
    94	    err.expose = status < 500
    95	    err.status = err.statusCode = status
    96	  }
    97	
    98	  for (var key in props) {
    99	    if (key !== 'status' && key !== 'statusCode') {
   100	      err[key] = props[key]
   101	    }
   102	  }
   103	
   104	  return err
   105	}
   106	
   107	/**
   108	 * Create HTTP error abstract base class.
   109	 * @private
   110	 */
   111	
   112	function createHttpErrorConstructor () {
   113	  function HttpError () {
   114	    throw new TypeError('cannot construct abstract class')
   115	  }
   116	
   117	  inherits(HttpError, Error)
   118	
   119	  return HttpError
   120	}
   121	
   122	/**
   123	 * Create a constructor for a client error.
   124	 * @private
   125	 */
   126	
   127	function createClientErrorConstructor (HttpError, name, code) {
   128	  var className = toClassName(name)
   129	
   130	  function ClientError (message) {
   131	    // create the error object
   132	    var msg = message != null ? message : statuses.message[code]
   133	    var err = new Error(msg)
   134	
   135	    // capture a stack trace to the construction point
   136	    Error.captureStackTrace(err, ClientError)
   137	
   138	    // adjust the [[Prototype]]
   139	    setPrototypeOf(err, ClientError.prototype)
   140	
   141	    // redefine the error message
   142	    Object.defineProperty(err, 'message', {
   143	      enumerable: true,
   144	      configurable: true,
   145	      value: msg,
   146	      writable: true
   147	    })
   148	
   149	    // redefine the error name
   150	    Object.defineProperty(err, 'name', {
   151	      enumerable: false,
   152	      configurable: true,
   153	      value: className,
   154	      writable: true
   155	    })
   156	
   157	    return err
   158	  }
   159	
   160	  inherits(ClientError, HttpError)
   161	  nameFunc(ClientError, className)
   162	
   163	  ClientError.prototype.status = code
   164	  ClientError.prototype.statusCode = code
   165	  ClientError.prototype.expose = true
   166	
   167	  return ClientError
   168	}
   169	
   170	/**
   171	 * Create function to test is a value is a HttpError.
   172	 * @private
   173	 */
   174	
   175	function createIsHttpErrorFunction (HttpError) {
   176	  return function isHttpError (val) {
   177	    if (!val || typeof val !== 'object') {
   178	      return false
   179	    }
   180	
   181	    if (val instanceof HttpError) {
   182	      return true
   183	    }
   184	
   185	    return val instanceof Error &&
   186	      typeof val.expose === 'boolean' &&
   187	      typeof val.statusCode === 'number' && val.status === val.statusCode
   188	  }
   189	}
   190	
   191	/**
   192	 * Create a constructor for a server error.
   193	 * @private
   194	 */
   195	
   196	function createServerErrorConstructor (HttpError, name, code) {
   197	  var className = toClassName(name)
   198	
   199	  function ServerError (message) {
   200	    // create the error object
   201	    var msg = message != null ? message : statuses.message[code]
   202	    var err = new Error(msg)
   203	
   204	    // capture a stack trace to the construction point
   205	    Error.captureStackTrace(err, ServerError)
   206	
   207	    // adjust the [[Prototype]]
   208	    setPrototypeOf(err, ServerError.prototype)
   209	
   210	    // redefine the error message
   211	    Object.defineProperty(err, 'message', {
   212	      enumerable: true,
   213	      configurable: true,
   214	      value: msg,
   215	      writable: true
   216	    })
   217	
   218	    // redefine the error name
   219	    Object.defineProperty(err, 'name', {
   220	      enumerable: false,
   221	      configurable: true,
   222	      value: className,
   223	      writable: true
   224	    })
   225	
   226	    return err
   227	  }
   228	
   229	  inherits(ServerError, HttpError)
   230	  nameFunc(ServerError, className)
   231	
   232	  ServerError.prototype.status = code
   233	  ServerError.prototype.statusCode = code
   234	  ServerError.prototype.expose = false
   235	
   236	  return ServerError
   237	}
   238	
   239	/**
   240	 * Set the name of a function, if possible.
   241	 * @private
   242	 */
   243	
   244	function nameFunc (func, name) {
   245	  var desc = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(func, 'name')
   246	
   247	  if (desc && desc.configurable) {
   248	    desc.value = name
   249	    Object.defineProperty(func, 'name', desc)
   250	  }
   251	}
   252	
   253	/**
   254	 * Populate the exports object with constructors for every error class.
   255	 * @private
   256	 */
   257	
   258	function populateConstructorExports (exports, codes, HttpError) {
   259	  codes.forEach(function forEachCode (code) {
   260	    var CodeError
   261	    var name = toIdentifier(statuses.message[code])
   262	
   263	    switch (codeClass(code)) {
   264	      case 400:
   265	        CodeError = createClientErrorConstructor(HttpError, name, code)
   266	        break
   267	      case 500:
   268	        CodeError = createServerErrorConstructor(HttpError, name, code)
   269	        break
   270	    }
   271	
   272	    if (CodeError) {
   273	      // export the constructor
   274	      exports[code] = CodeError
   275	      exports[name] = CodeError
   276	    }
   277	  })
   278	}
   279	
   280	/**
   281	 * Get a class name from a name identifier.
   282	 *
   283	 * @param {string} name
   284	 * @returns {string}
   285	 * @private
   286	 */
   287	
   288	function toClassName (name) {
   289	  return name.slice(-5) === 'Error' ? name : name + 'Error'
   290	}

     1	# http-errors
     2	
     3	[![NPM Version][npm-version-image]][npm-url]
     4	[![NPM Downloads][npm-downloads-image]][node-url]
     5	[![Node.js Version][node-image]][node-url]
     6	[![Build Status][ci-image]][ci-url]
     7	[![Test Coverage][coveralls-image]][coveralls-url]
     8	
     9	Create HTTP errors for Express, Koa, Connect, etc. with ease.
    10	
    11	## Install
    12	
    13	This is a [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/) module available through the
    14	[npm registry](https://www.npmjs.com/). Installation is done using the
    15	[`npm install` command](https://docs.npmjs.com/getting-started/installing-npm-packages-locally):
    16	
    17	```console
    18	$ npm install http-errors
    19	```
    20	
    21	## Example
    22	
    23	```js
    24	var createError = require('http-errors')
    25	var express = require('express')
    26	var app = express()
    27	
    28	app.use(function (req, res, next) {
    29	  if (!req.user) return next(createError(401, 'Please login to view this page.'))
    30	  next()
    31	})
    32	```
    33	
    34	## API
    35	
    36	This is the current API, currently extracted from Koa and subject to change.
    37	
    38	### Error Properties
    39	
    40	- `expose` - can be used to signal if `message` should be sent to the client,
    41	  defaulting to `false` when `status` >= 500
    42	- `headers` - can be an object of header names to values to be sent to the
    43	  client, defaulting to `undefined`. When defined, the key names should all
    44	  be lower-cased
    45	- `message` - the traditional error message, which should be kept short and all
    46	  single line
    47	- `status` - the status code of the error, mirroring `statusCode` for general
    48	  compatibility
    49	- `statusCode` - the status code of the error, defaulting to `500`
    50	
    51	### createError([status], [message], [properties])
    52	
    53	Create a new error object with the given message `msg`.
    54	The error object inherits from `createError.HttpError`.
    55	
    56	```js
    57	var err = createError(404, 'This video does not exist!')
    58	```
    59	
    60	- `status: 500` - the status code as a number
    61	- `message` - the message of the error, defaulting to node's text for that status code.
    62	- `properties` - custom properties to attach to the object
    63	
    64	### createError([status], [error], [properties])
    65	
    66	Extend the given `error` object with `createError.HttpError`
    67	properties. This will not alter the inheritance of the given
    68	`error` object, and the modified `error` object is the
    69	return value.
    70	
    71	<!-- eslint-disable no-redeclare -->
    72	
    73	```js
    74	fs.readFile('foo.txt', function (err, buf) {
    75	  if (err) {
    76	    if (err.code === 'ENOENT') {
    77	      var httpError = createError(404, err, { expose: false })
    78	    } else {
    79	      var httpError = createError(500, err)
    80	    }
    81	  }
    82	})
    83	```
    84	
    85	- `status` - the status code as a number
    86	- `error` - the error object to extend
    87	- `properties` - custom properties to attach to the object
    88	
    89	### createError.isHttpError(val)
    90	
    91	Determine if the provided `val` is an `HttpError`. This will return `true`
    92	if the error inherits from the `HttpError` constructor of this module or
    93	matches the "duck type" for an error this module creates. All outputs from
    94	the `createError` factory will return `true` for this function, including
    95	if an non-`HttpError` was passed into the factory.
    96	
    97	### new createError\[code || name\](\[msg]\))
    98	
    99	Create a new error object with the given message `msg`.
   100	The error object inherits from `createError.HttpError`.
   101	
   102	```js
   103	var err = new createError.NotFound()
   104	```
   105	
   106	- `code` - the status code as a number
   107	- `name` - the name of the error as a "bumpy case", i.e. `NotFound` or `InternalServerError`.
   108	
   109	#### List of all constructors
