   823	  /**
   824	   * The base implementation of `_.map` without support for iteratee shorthands.
   825	   *
   826	   * @private
   827	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to iterate over.
   828	   * @param {Function} iteratee The function invoked per iteration.
   829	   * @returns {Array} Returns the new mapped array.
   830	   */
   831	  function baseMap(collection, iteratee) {
   832	    var index = -1,
   833	        result = isArrayLike(collection) ? Array(collection.length) : [];
   834	
   835	    baseEach(collection, function(value, key, collection) {
   836	      result[++index] = iteratee(value, key, collection);
   837	    });
   838	    return result;
   839	  }
   840	
   841	  /**
   842	   * The base implementation of `_.matches` which doesn't clone `source`.
   843	   *
   844	   * @private
   845	   * @param {Object} source The object of property values to match.
   846	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new spec function.
   847	   */
   848	  function baseMatches(source) {
   849	    var props = keys(source);
   850	    return function(object) {
   851	      var length = props.length;
   852	      if (object == null) {
   853	        return !length;
   854	      }
   855	      object = Object(object);
   856	      while (length--) {
   857	        var key = props[length];
   858	        if (!(key in object &&
   859	              baseIsEqual(source[key], object[key], undefined, UNORDERED_COMPARE_FLAG | PARTIAL_COMPARE_FLAG)
   860	            )) {
   861	          return false;
   862	        }
   863	      }
   864	      return true;
   865	    };
   866	  }
   867	
   868	  /**
   869	   * The base implementation of `_.pick` without support for individual
   870	   * property identifiers.
   871	   *
   872	   * @private
   873	   * @param {Object} object The source object.
   874	   * @param {string[]} props The property identifiers to pick.
   875	   * @returns {Object} Returns the new object.
   876	   */
   877	  function basePick(object, props) {
   878	    object = Object(object);
   879	    return reduce(props, function(result, key) {
   880	      if (key in object) {
   881	        result[key] = object[key];
   882	      }
   883	      return result;
   884	    }, {});
   885	  }
   886	
   887	  /**
   888	   * The base implementation of `_.property` without support for deep paths.
   889	   *
   890	   * @private
   891	   * @param {string} key The key of the property to get.
   892	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new accessor function.
   893	   */
   894	  function baseProperty(key) {
   895	    return function(object) {
   896	      return object == null ? undefined : object[key];
   897	    };
   898	  }
   899	
   900	  /**
   901	   * The base implementation of `_.slice` without an iteratee call guard.
   902	   *
   903	   * @private
   904	   * @param {Array} array The array to slice.
   905	   * @param {number} [start=0] The start position.
   906	   * @param {number} [end=array.length] The end position.
   907	   * @returns {Array} Returns the slice of `array`.
   908	   */
   909	  function baseSlice(array, start, end) {
   910	    var index = -1,
   911	        length = array.length;
   912	
   913	    if (start < 0) {
   914	      start = -start > length ? 0 : (length + start);
   915	    }
   916	    end = end > length ? length : end;
   917	    if (end < 0) {
   918	      end += length;
   919	    }
   920	    length = start > end ? 0 : ((end - start) >>> 0);
   921	    start >>>= 0;
   922	
   923	    var result = Array(length);
   924	    while (++index < length) {
   925	      result[index] = array[index + start];
   926	    }
   927	    return result;
   928	  }
   929	
   930	  /**
   931	   * Copies the values of `source` to `array`.
   932	   *
   933	   * @private
   934	   * @param {Array} source The array to copy values from.
   935	   * @param {Array} [array=[]] The array to copy values to.
   936	   * @returns {Array} Returns `array`.
   937	   */
   938	  function copyArray(source) {
   939	    return baseSlice(source, 0, source.length);
   940	  }
   941	
   942	  /**
   943	   * The base implementation of `_.some` without support for iteratee shorthands.
   944	   *
   945	   * @private
   946	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to iterate over.
   947	   * @param {Function} predicate The function invoked per iteration.
   948	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if any element passes the predicate check,
   949	   *  else `false`.
   950	   */
   951	  function baseSome(collection, predicate) {
   952	    var result;
   953	
   954	    baseEach(collection, function(value, index, collection) {
   955	      result = predicate(value, index, collection);
   956	      return !result;
   957	    });
   958	    return !!result;
   959	  }
   960	
   961	  /**
   962	   * The base implementation of `wrapperValue` which returns the result of
   963	   * performing a sequence of actions on the unwrapped `value`, where each
   964	   * successive action is supplied the return value of the previous.
   965	   *
   966	   * @private
   967	   * @param {*} value The unwrapped value.
   968	   * @param {Array} actions Actions to perform to resolve the unwrapped value.
   969	   * @returns {*} Returns the resolved value.
   970	   */
   971	  function baseWrapperValue(value, actions) {
   972	    var result = value;
   973	    return reduce(actions, function(result, action) {
   974	      return action.func.apply(action.thisArg, arrayPush([result], action.args));
   975	    }, result);
   976	  }
   977	
   978	  /**
   979	   * Compares values to sort them in ascending order.
   980	   *
   981	   * @private
   982	   * @param {*} value The value to compare.
   983	   * @param {*} other The other value to compare.
   984	   * @returns {number} Returns the sort order indicator for `value`.
   985	   */
   986	  function compareAscending(value, other) {
   987	    if (value !== other) {
   988	      var valIsDefined = value !== undefined,
   989	          valIsNull = value === null,
   990	          valIsReflexive = value === value,
   991	          valIsSymbol = false;
   992	
   993	      var othIsDefined = other !== undefined,
   994	          othIsNull = other === null,
   995	          othIsReflexive = other === other,
   996	          othIsSymbol = false;
   997	
   998	      if ((!othIsNull && !othIsSymbol && !valIsSymbol && value > other) ||
   999	          (valIsSymbol && othIsDefined && othIsReflexive && !othIsNull && !othIsSymbol) ||
  1000	          (valIsNull && othIsDefined && othIsReflexive) ||
  1001	          (!valIsDefined && othIsReflexive) ||
  1002	          !valIsReflexive) {
  1003	        return 1;
  1004	      }
  1005	      if ((!valIsNull && !valIsSymbol && !othIsSymbol && value < other) ||
  1006	          (othIsSymbol && valIsDefined && valIsReflexive && !valIsNull && !valIsSymbol) ||
  1007	          (othIsNull && valIsDefined && valIsReflexive) ||
  1008	          (!othIsDefined && valIsReflexive) ||
  1009	          !othIsReflexive) {
  1010	        return -1;
  1011	      }
  1012	    }
  1013	    return 0;
  1014	  }
  1015	
  1016	  /**
  1017	   * Copies properties of `source` to `object`.
  1018	   *
  1019	   * @private
  1020	   * @param {Object} source The object to copy properties from.
  1021	   * @param {Array} props The property identifiers to copy.
  1022	   * @param {Object} [object={}] The object to copy properties to.
  1023	   * @param {Function} [customizer] The function to customize copied values.
  1024	   * @returns {Object} Returns `object`.
  1025	   */
  1026	  function copyObject(source, props, object, customizer) {
  1027	    object || (object = {});
  1028	
  1029	    var index = -1,
  1030	        length = props.length;
  1031	
  1032	    while (++index < length) {
  1033	      var key = props[index];
  1034	
  1035	      var newValue = customizer
  1036	        ? customizer(object[key], source[key], key, object, source)
  1037	        : source[key];
  1038	
  1039	      assignValue(object, key, newValue);
  1040	    }
  1041	    return object;
  1042	  }
  1043	
  1044	  /**
  1045	   * Creates a function like `_.assign`.
  1046	   *
  1047	   * @private
  1048	   * @param {Function} assigner The function to assign values.
  1049	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new assigner function.
  1050	   */
  1051	  function createAssigner(assigner) {
  1052	    return rest(function(object, sources) {
  1053	      var index = -1,
  1054	          length = sources.length,
  1055	          customizer = length > 1 ? sources[length - 1] : undefined;
  1056	
  1057	      customizer = (assigner.length > 3 && typeof customizer == 'function')
  1058	        ? (length--, customizer)
  1059	        : undefined;
  1060	
  1061	      object = Object(object);
  1062	      while (++index < length) {
  1063	        var source = sources[index];
  1064	        if (source) {
  1065	          assigner(object, source, index, customizer);
  1066	        }
  1067	      }
  1068	      return object;
  1069	    });
  1070	  }
  1071	
  1072	  /**
  1073	   * Creates a `baseEach` or `baseEachRight` function.
  1074	   *
  1075	   * @private
  1076	   * @param {Function} eachFunc The function to iterate over a collection.
  1077	   * @param {boolean} [fromRight] Specify iterating from right to left.
  1078	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new base function.
  1079	   */
  1080	  function createBaseEach(eachFunc, fromRight) {
  1081	    return function(collection, iteratee) {
  1082	      if (collection == null) {
  1083	        return collection;
  1084	      }
  1085	      if (!isArrayLike(collection)) {
  1086	        return eachFunc(collection, iteratee);
  1087	      }
  1088	      var length = collection.length,
  1089	          index = fromRight ? length : -1,
  1090	          iterable = Object(collection);
  1091	
  1092	      while ((fromRight ? index-- : ++index < length)) {
  1093	        if (iteratee(iterable[index], index, iterable) === false) {
  1094	          break;
  1095	        }
  1096	      }
  1097	      return collection;
  1098	    };
  1099	  }
  1100	
  1101	  /**
  1102	   * Creates a base function for methods like `_.forIn` and `_.forOwn`.
  1103	   *
  1104	   * @private
  1105	   * @param {boolean} [fromRight] Specify iterating from right to left.
  1106	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new base function.
  1107	   */
  1108	  function createBaseFor(fromRight) {
  1109	    return function(object, iteratee, keysFunc) {
  1110	      var index = -1,
  1111	          iterable = Object(object),
  1112	          props = keysFunc(object),
  1113	          length = props.length;
  1114	
  1115	      while (length--) {
  1116	        var key = props[fromRight ? length : ++index];
  1117	        if (iteratee(iterable[key], key, iterable) === false) {
  1118	          break;
  1119	        }
  1120	      }
  1121	      return object;
  1122	    };
  1123	  }
  1124	
  1125	  /**
  1126	   * Creates a function that produces an instance of `Ctor` regardless of
  1127	   * whether it was invoked as part of a `new` expression or by `call` or `apply`.
  1128	   *
  1129	   * @private
  1130	   * @param {Function} Ctor The constructor to wrap.
  1131	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new wrapped function.
  1132	   */
  1133	  function createCtorWrapper(Ctor) {
  1134	    return function() {
  1135	      // Use a `switch` statement to work with class constructors. See
  1136	      // http://ecma-international.org/ecma-262/6.0/#sec-ecmascript-function-objects-call-thisargument-argumentslist
  1137	      // for more details.
  1138	      var args = arguments;
  1139	      var thisBinding = baseCreate(Ctor.prototype),
  1140	          result = Ctor.apply(thisBinding, args);
  1141	
  1142	      // Mimic the constructor's `return` behavior.
  1143	      // See https://es5.github.io/#x13.2.2 for more details.
  1144	      return isObject(result) ? result : thisBinding;
  1145	    };
  1146	  }
  1147	
  1148	  /**
  1149	   * Creates a function that wraps `func` to invoke it with the `this` binding
  1150	   * of `thisArg` and `partials` prepended to the arguments it receives.
  1151	   *
  1152	   * @private
  1153	   * @param {Function} func The function to wrap.
  1154	   * @param {number} bitmask The bitmask of wrapper flags. See `createWrapper`
  1155	   *  for more details.
  1156	   * @param {*} thisArg The `this` binding of `func`.
  1157	   * @param {Array} partials The arguments to prepend to those provided to
  1158	   *  the new function.
  1159	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new wrapped function.
  1160	   */
  1161	  function createPartialWrapper(func, bitmask, thisArg, partials) {
  1162	    if (typeof func != 'function') {
  1163	      throw new TypeError(FUNC_ERROR_TEXT);
  1164	    }
  1165	    var isBind = bitmask & BIND_FLAG,
  1166	        Ctor = createCtorWrapper(func);
  1167	
  1168	    function wrapper() {
  1169	      var argsIndex = -1,
  1170	          argsLength = arguments.length,
  1171	          leftIndex = -1,
  1172	          leftLength = partials.length,
  1173	          args = Array(leftLength + argsLength),
  1174	          fn = (this && this !== root && this instanceof wrapper) ? Ctor : func;
  1175	
  1176	      while (++leftIndex < leftLength) {
  1177	        args[leftIndex] = partials[leftIndex];
  1178	      }
  1179	      while (argsLength--) {
  1180	        args[leftIndex++] = arguments[++argsIndex];
  1181	      }
  1182	      return fn.apply(isBind ? thisArg : this, args);
  1183	    }
  1184	    return wrapper;
  1185	  }
  1186	
  1187	  /**
  1188	   * A specialized version of `baseIsEqualDeep` for arrays with support for
  1189	   * partial deep comparisons.
  1190	   *
  1191	   * @private
  1192	   * @param {Array} array The array to compare.
  1193	   * @param {Array} other The other array to compare.
  1194	   * @param {Function} equalFunc The function to determine equivalents of values.
  1195	   * @param {Function} customizer The function to customize comparisons.
  1196	   * @param {number} bitmask The bitmask of comparison flags. See `baseIsEqual`
  1197	   *  for more details.
  1198	   * @param {Object} stack Tracks traversed `array` and `other` objects.
  1199	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if the arrays are equivalent, else `false`.
  1200	   */
  1201	  function equalArrays(array, other, equalFunc, customizer, bitmask, stack) {
  1202	    var isPartial = bitmask & PARTIAL_COMPARE_FLAG,
  1203	        arrLength = array.length,
  1204	        othLength = other.length;
  1205	
  1206	    if (arrLength != othLength && !(isPartial && othLength > arrLength)) {
  1207	      return false;
  1208	    }
  1209	    var index = -1,
  1210	        result = true,
  1211	        seen = (bitmask & UNORDERED_COMPARE_FLAG) ? [] : undefined;
  1212	
  1213	    // Ignore non-index properties.
  1214	    while (++index < arrLength) {
  1215	      var arrValue = array[index],
  1216	          othValue = other[index];
  1217	
  1218	      var compared;
  1219	      if (compared !== undefined) {
  1220	        if (compared) {
  1221	          continue;
  1222	        }
  1223	        result = false;
  1224	        break;
  1225	      }
  1226	      // Recursively compare arrays (susceptible to call stack limits).
  1227	      if (seen) {
  1228	        if (!baseSome(other, function(othValue, othIndex) {
  1229	              if (!indexOf(seen, othIndex) &&
  1230	                  (arrValue === othValue || equalFunc(arrValue, othValue, customizer, bitmask, stack))) {
  1231	                return seen.push(othIndex);
  1232	              }
  1233	            })) {
  1234	          result = false;
  1235	          break;
  1236	        }
  1237	      } else if (!(
  1238	            arrValue === othValue ||
  1239	              equalFunc(arrValue, othValue, customizer, bitmask, stack)
  1240	          )) {
  1241	        result = false;
  1242	        break;
  1243	      }
  1244	    }
  1245	    return result;
  1246	  }
  1247	
  1248	  /**
  1249	   * A specialized version of `baseIsEqualDeep` for comparing objects of
  1250	   * the same `toStringTag`.
  1251	   *
  1252	   * **Note:** This function only supports comparing values with tags of
  1253	   * `Boolean`, `Date`, `Error`, `Number`, `RegExp`, or `String`.
  1254	   *
  1255	   * @private
  1256	   * @param {Object} object The object to compare.
  1257	   * @param {Object} other The other object to compare.
  1258	   * @param {string} tag The `toStringTag` of the objects to compare.
  1259	   * @param {Function} equalFunc The function to determine equivalents of values.
  1260	   * @param {Function} customizer The function to customize comparisons.
  1261	   * @param {number} bitmask The bitmask of comparison flags. See `baseIsEqual`
  1262	   *  for more details.
  1263	   * @param {Object} stack Tracks traversed `object` and `other` objects.
  1264	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if the objects are equivalent, else `false`.
  1265	   */
  1266	  function equalByTag(object, other, tag, equalFunc, customizer, bitmask, stack) {
  1267	    switch (tag) {
  1268	
  1269	      case boolTag:
  1270	      case dateTag:
  1271	        // Coerce dates and booleans to numbers, dates to milliseconds and
  1272	        // booleans to `1` or `0` treating invalid dates coerced to `NaN` as
  1273	        // not equal.
  1274	        return +object == +other;
  1275	
  1276	      case errorTag:
  1277	        return object.name == other.name && object.message == other.message;
  1278	
  1279	      case numberTag:
  1280	        // Treat `NaN` vs. `NaN` as equal.
  1281	        return (object != +object) ? other != +other : object == +other;
  1282	
  1283	      case regexpTag:
  1284	      case stringTag:
  1285	        // Coerce regexes to strings and treat strings, primitives and objects,
  1286	        // as equal. See http://www.ecma-international.org/ecma-262/6.0/#sec-regexp.prototype.tostring
  1287	        // for more details.
  1288	        return object == (other + '');
  1289	
  1290	    }
  1291	    return false;
  1292	  }
  1293	
  1294	  /**
  1295	   * A specialized version of `baseIsEqualDeep` for objects with support for
  1296	   * partial deep comparisons.
  1297	   *
  1298	   * @private
  1299	   * @param {Object} object The object to compare.
  1300	   * @param {Object} other The other object to compare.
  1301	   * @param {Function} equalFunc The function to determine equivalents of values.
  1302	   * @param {Function} customizer The function to customize comparisons.
  1303	   * @param {number} bitmask The bitmask of comparison flags. See `baseIsEqual`
  1304	   *  for more details.
  1305	   * @param {Object} stack Tracks traversed `object` and `other` objects.
  1306	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if the objects are equivalent, else `false`.
  1307	   */
  1308	  function equalObjects(object, other, equalFunc, customizer, bitmask, stack) {
  1309	    var isPartial = bitmask & PARTIAL_COMPARE_FLAG,
  1310	        objProps = keys(object),
  1311	        objLength = objProps.length,
  1312	        othProps = keys(other),
  1313	        othLength = othProps.length;
  1314	
  1315	    if (objLength != othLength && !isPartial) {
  1316	      return false;
  1317	    }
  1318	    var index = objLength;
  1319	    while (index--) {
  1320	      var key = objProps[index];
  1321	      if (!(isPartial ? key in other : hasOwnProperty.call(other, key))) {
  1322	        return false;
  1323	      }
  1324	    }
  1325	    var result = true;
  1326	
  1327	    var skipCtor = isPartial;
  1328	    while (++index < objLength) {
  1329	      key = objProps[index];
  1330	      var objValue = object[key],
  1331	          othValue = other[key];
  1332	
  1333	      var compared;
  1334	      // Recursively compare objects (susceptible to call stack limits).
  1335	      if (!(compared === undefined
  1336	            ? (objValue === othValue || equalFunc(objValue, othValue, customizer, bitmask, stack))
  1337	            : compared
  1338	          )) {
  1339	        result = false;
  1340	        break;
  1341	      }
  1342	      skipCtor || (skipCtor = key == 'constructor');
  1343	    }
  1344	    if (result && !skipCtor) {
  1345	      var objCtor = object.constructor,
  1346	          othCtor = other.constructor;
  1347	
  1348	      // Non `Object` object instances with different constructors are not equal.
  1349	      if (objCtor != othCtor &&
  1350	          ('constructor' in object && 'constructor' in other) &&
  1351	          !(typeof objCtor == 'function' && objCtor instanceof objCtor &&
  1352	            typeof othCtor == 'function' && othCtor instanceof othCtor)) {
  1353	        result = false;
  1354	      }
  1355	    }
  1356	    return result;
  1357	  }

  1400	  /**
  1401	   * Checks if `value` is a valid array-like index.
  1402	   *
  1403	   * @private
  1404	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  1405	   * @param {number} [length=MAX_SAFE_INTEGER] The upper bounds of a valid index.
  1406	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is a valid index, else `false`.
  1407	   */
  1408	  function isIndex(value, length) {
  1409	    length = length == null ? MAX_SAFE_INTEGER : length;
  1410	    return !!length &&
  1411	      (typeof value == 'number' || reIsUint.test(value)) &&
  1412	      (value > -1 && value % 1 == 0 && value < length);
  1413	  }

  1424	        proto = (typeof Ctor == 'function' && Ctor.prototype) || objectProto;

  1459	  /**
  1460	   * Creates a new array concatenating `array` with any additional arrays
  1461	   * and/or values.
  1462	   *
  1463	   * @static
  1464	   * @memberOf _
  1465	   * @since 4.0.0
  1466	   * @category Array
  1467	   * @param {Array} array The array to concatenate.
  1468	   * @param {...*} [values] The values to concatenate.
  1469	   * @returns {Array} Returns the new concatenated array.
  1470	   * @example
  1471	   *
  1472	   * var array = [1];
  1473	   * var other = _.concat(array, 2, [3], [[4]]);
  1474	   *
  1475	   * console.log(other);
  1476	   * // => [1, 2, 3, [4]]
  1477	   *
  1478	   * console.log(array);
  1479	   * // => [1]
  1480	   */
  1481	  function concat() {
  1482	    var length = arguments.length,
  1483	        args = Array(length ? length - 1 : 0),
  1484	        array = arguments[0],
  1485	        index = length;
  1486	
  1487	    while (index--) {
  1488	      args[index - 1] = arguments[index];
  1489	    }
  1490	    return length
  1491	      ? arrayPush(isArray(array) ? copyArray(array) : [array], baseFlatten(args, 1))
  1492	      : [];
  1493	  }

  1551	  function head(array) {

  1553	  }

  1555	  /**
  1556	   * Gets the index at which the first occurrence of `value` is found in `array`
  1557	   * using [`SameValueZero`](http://ecma-international.org/ecma-262/6.0/#sec-samevaluezero)
  1558	   * for equality comparisons. If `fromIndex` is negative, it's used as the
  1559	   * offset from the end of `array`.
  1560	   *
  1561	   * @static
  1562	   * @memberOf _
  1563	   * @since 0.1.0
  1564	   * @category Array
  1565	   * @param {Array} array The array to search.
  1566	   * @param {*} value The value to search for.
  1567	   * @param {number} [fromIndex=0] The index to search from.
  1568	   * @returns {number} Returns the index of the matched value, else `-1`.
  1569	   * @example
  1570	   *
  1571	   * _.indexOf([1, 2, 1, 2], 2);
  1572	   * // => 1
  1573	   *
  1574	   * // Search from the `fromIndex`.
  1575	   * _.indexOf([1, 2, 1, 2], 2, 2);
  1576	   * // => 3
  1577	   */
  1578	  function indexOf(array, value, fromIndex) {
  1579	    var length = array ? array.length : 0;
  1580	    if (typeof fromIndex == 'number') {
  1581	      fromIndex = fromIndex < 0 ? nativeMax(length + fromIndex, 0) : fromIndex;
  1582	    } else {
  1583	      fromIndex = 0;
  1584	    }
  1585	    var index = (fromIndex || 0) - 1,
  1586	        isReflexive = value === value;
  1587	
  1588	    while (++index < length) {
  1589	      var other = array[index];
  1590	      if ((isReflexive ? other === value : other !== other)) {
  1591	        return index;
  1592	      }
  1593	    }
  1594	    return -1;
  1595	  }

  1598	   * Gets the last element of `array`.

  1604	   * @param {Array} array The array to query.
  1605	   * @returns {*} Returns the last element of `array`.
  1606	   * @example
  1607	   *
  1608	   * _.last([1, 2, 3]);
  1609	   * // => 3
  1610	   */
  1611	  function last(array) {
  1612	    var length = array ? array.length : 0;

  1618	   *
  1619	   * **Note:** This method is used instead of

  1621	   * returned.
  1622	   *
  1623	   * @static
  1624	   * @memberOf _
  1625	   * @since 3.0.0

  1641	  /**
  1642	   * Creates a `lodash` wrapper instance that wraps `value` with explicit method
  1643	   * chain sequences enabled. The result of such sequences must be unwrapped
  1644	   * with `_#value`.
  1645	   *
  1646	   * @static
  1647	   * @memberOf _
  1648	   * @since 1.3.0
  1649	   * @category Seq
  1650	   * @param {*} value The value to wrap.
  1651	   * @returns {Object} Returns the new `lodash` wrapper instance.
  1652	   * @example
  1653	   *
  1654	   * var users = [
  1655	   *   { 'user': 'barney',  'age': 36 },
  1656	   *   { 'user': 'fred',    'age': 40 },
  1657	   *   { 'user': 'pebbles', 'age': 1 }
  1658	   * ];
  1659	   *
  1660	   * var youngest = _
  1661	   *   .chain(users)
  1662	   *   .sortBy('age')
  1663	   *   .map(function(o) {
  1664	   *     return o.user + ' is ' + o.age;
  1665	   *   })
  1666	   *   .head()
  1667	   *   .value();
  1668	   * // => 'pebbles is 1'
  1669	   */
  1670	  function chain(value) {
  1671	    var result = lodash(value);
  1672	    result.__chain__ = true;
  1673	    return result;
  1674	  }
  1675	
  1676	  /**
  1677	   * This method invokes `interceptor` and returns `value`. The interceptor
  1678	   * is invoked with one argument; (value). The purpose of this method is to
  1679	   * "tap into" a method chain sequence in order to modify intermediate results.
  1680	   *
  1681	   * @static
  1682	   * @memberOf _
  1683	   * @since 0.1.0
  1684	   * @category Seq
  1685	   * @param {*} value The value to provide to `interceptor`.
  1686	   * @param {Function} interceptor The function to invoke.
  1687	   * @returns {*} Returns `value`.
  1688	   * @example
  1689	   *
  1690	   * _([1, 2, 3])
  1691	   *  .tap(function(array) {
  1692	   *    // Mutate input array.
  1693	   *    array.pop();
  1694	   *  })
  1695	   *  .reverse()
  1696	   *  .value();
  1697	   * // => [2, 1]
  1698	   */
  1699	  function tap(value, interceptor) {
  1700	    interceptor(value);
  1701	    return value;
  1702	  }
  1703	
  1704	  /**
  1705	   * This method is like `_.tap` except that it returns the result of `interceptor`.
  1706	   * The purpose of this method is to "pass thru" values replacing intermediate
  1707	   * results in a method chain sequence.
  1708	   *
  1709	   * @static
  1710	   * @memberOf _
  1711	   * @since 3.0.0
  1712	   * @category Seq
  1713	   * @param {*} value The value to provide to `interceptor`.
  1714	   * @param {Function} interceptor The function to invoke.
  1715	   * @returns {*} Returns the result of `interceptor`.
  1716	   * @example
  1717	   *
  1718	   * _('  abc  ')
  1719	   *  .chain()
  1720	   *  .trim()
  1721	   *  .thru(function(value) {
  1722	   *    return [value];
  1723	   *  })
  1724	   *  .value();
  1725	   * // => ['abc']
  1726	   */
  1727	  function thru(value, interceptor) {
  1728	    return interceptor(value);
  1729	  }
  1730	
  1731	  /**
  1732	   * Creates a `lodash` wrapper instance with explicit method chain sequences enabled.
  1733	   *
  1734	   * @name chain
  1735	   * @memberOf _
  1736	   * @since 0.1.0
  1737	   * @category Seq
  1738	   * @returns {Object} Returns the new `lodash` wrapper instance.
  1739	   * @example
  1740	   *
  1741	   * var users = [
  1742	   *   { 'user': 'barney', 'age': 36 },
  1743	   *   { 'user': 'fred',   'age': 40 }
  1744	   * ];
  1745	   *
  1746	   * // A sequence without explicit chaining.
  1747	   * _(users).head();
  1748	   * // => { 'user': 'barney', 'age': 36 }
  1749	   *
  1750	   * // A sequence with explicit chaining.
  1751	   * _(users)
  1752	   *   .chain()
  1753	   *   .head()
  1754	   *   .pick('user')
  1755	   *   .value();
  1756	   * // => { 'user': 'barney' }
  1757	   */
  1758	  function wrapperChain() {
  1759	    return chain(this);
  1760	  }
  1761	
  1762	  /**
  1763	   * Executes the chain sequence to resolve the unwrapped value.
  1764	   *
  1765	   * @name value
  1766	   * @memberOf _
  1767	   * @since 0.1.0
  1768	   * @alias toJSON, valueOf
  1769	   * @category Seq
  1770	   * @returns {*} Returns the resolved unwrapped value.
  1771	   * @example
  1772	   *
  1773	   * _([1, 2, 3]).value();
  1774	   * // => [1, 2, 3]
  1775	   */
  1776	  function wrapperValue() {
  1777	    return baseWrapperValue(this.__wrapped__, this.__actions__);
  1778	  }

  1781	
  1782	  /**
  1783	   * Checks if `predicate` returns truthy for **all** elements of `collection`.
  1784	   * Iteration is stopped once `predicate` returns falsey. The predicate is
  1785	   * invoked with three arguments: (value, index|key, collection).
  1786	   *
  1787	   * @static
  1788	   * @memberOf _
  1789	   * @since 0.1.0
  1790	   * @category Collection
  1791	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to iterate over.
  1792	   * @param {Array|Function|Object|string} [predicate=_.identity]
  1793	   *  The function invoked per iteration.
  1794	   * @param- {Object} [guard] Enables use as an iteratee for methods like `_.map`.
  1795	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if all elements pass the predicate check,
  1796	   *  else `false`.
  1797	   * @example
  1798	   *
  1799	   * _.every([true, 1, null, 'yes'], Boolean);
  1800	   * // => false
  1801	   *
  1802	   * var users = [
  1803	   *   { 'user': 'barney', 'age': 36, 'active': false },
  1804	   *   { 'user': 'fred',   'age': 40, 'active': false }
  1805	   * ];
  1806	   *
  1807	   * // The `_.matches` iteratee shorthand.
  1808	   * _.every(users, { 'user': 'barney', 'active': false });
  1809	   * // => false
  1810	   *
  1811	   * // The `_.matchesProperty` iteratee shorthand.
  1812	   * _.every(users, ['active', false]);
  1813	   * // => true
  1814	   *
  1815	   * // The `_.property` iteratee shorthand.
  1816	   * _.every(users, 'active');
  1817	   * // => false
  1818	   */
  1819	  function every(collection, predicate, guard) {
  1820	    predicate = guard ? undefined : predicate;
  1821	    return baseEvery(collection, baseIteratee(predicate));
  1822	  }
  1823	
  1824	  /**
  1825	   * Iterates over elements of `collection`, returning an array of all elements
  1826	   * `predicate` returns truthy for. The predicate is invoked with three
  1827	   * arguments: (value, index|key, collection).
  1828	   *
  1829	   * @static
  1830	   * @memberOf _
  1831	   * @since 0.1.0
  1832	   * @category Collection
  1833	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to iterate over.
  1834	   * @param {Array|Function|Object|string} [predicate=_.identity]
  1835	   *  The function invoked per iteration.
  1836	   * @returns {Array} Returns the new filtered array.
  1837	   * @see _.reject
  1838	   * @example
  1839	   *
  1840	   * var users = [
  1841	   *   { 'user': 'barney', 'age': 36, 'active': true },
  1842	   *   { 'user': 'fred',   'age': 40, 'active': false }
  1843	   * ];
  1844	   *
  1845	   * _.filter(users, function(o) { return !o.active; });
  1846	   * // => objects for ['fred']
  1847	   *
  1848	   * // The `_.matches` iteratee shorthand.
  1849	   * _.filter(users, { 'age': 36, 'active': true });
  1850	   * // => objects for ['barney']
  1851	   *
  1852	   * // The `_.matchesProperty` iteratee shorthand.
  1853	   * _.filter(users, ['active', false]);
  1854	   * // => objects for ['fred']
  1855	   *
  1856	   * // The `_.property` iteratee shorthand.
  1857	   * _.filter(users, 'active');
  1858	   * // => objects for ['barney']
  1859	   */
  1860	  function filter(collection, predicate) {
  1861	    return baseFilter(collection, baseIteratee(predicate));
  1862	  }
  1863	
  1864	  /**
  1865	   * Iterates over elements of `collection`, returning the first element
  1866	   * `predicate` returns truthy for. The predicate is invoked with three
  1867	   * arguments: (value, index|key, collection).
  1868	   *
  1869	   * @static
  1870	   * @memberOf _
  1871	   * @since 0.1.0
  1872	   * @category Collection
  1873	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to search.
  1874	   * @param {Array|Function|Object|string} [predicate=_.identity]
  1875	   *  The function invoked per iteration.
  1876	   * @returns {*} Returns the matched element, else `undefined`.
  1877	   * @example
  1878	   *
  1879	   * var users = [
  1880	   *   { 'user': 'barney',  'age': 36, 'active': true },
  1881	   *   { 'user': 'fred',    'age': 40, 'active': false },
  1882	   *   { 'user': 'pebbles', 'age': 1,  'active': true }
  1883	   * ];

  1885	   * _.find(users, function(o) { return o.age < 40; });
  1886	   * // => object for 'barney'
  1887	   *
  1888	   * // The `_.matches` iteratee shorthand.
  1889	   * _.find(users, { 'age': 1, 'active': true });
  1890	   * // => object for 'pebbles'

  1892	   * // The `_.matchesProperty` iteratee shorthand.
  1893	   * _.find(users, ['active', false]);
  1894	   * // => object for 'fred'
  1895	   *
  1896	   * // The `_.property` iteratee shorthand.
  1897	   * _.find(users, 'active');
  1898	   * // => object for 'barney'
  1899	   */
  1900	  function find(collection, predicate) {
  1901	    return baseFind(collection, baseIteratee(predicate), baseEach);
  1902	  }
  1903	
  1904	  /**
  1905	   * Iterates over elements of `collection` and invokes `iteratee` for each element.
  1906	   * The iteratee is invoked with three arguments: (value, index|key, collection).
  1907	   * Iteratee functions may exit iteration early by explicitly returning `false`.
  1908	   *
  1909	   * **Note:** As with other "Collections" methods, objects with a "length"
  1910	   * property are iterated like arrays. To avoid this behavior use `_.forIn`
  1911	   * or `_.forOwn` for object iteration.
  1912	   *
  1913	   * @static
  1914	   * @memberOf _
  1915	   * @since 0.1.0
  1916	   * @alias each
  1917	   * @category Collection
  1918	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to iterate over.
  1919	   * @param {Function} [iteratee=_.identity] The function invoked per iteration.
  1920	   * @returns {Array|Object} Returns `collection`.
  1921	   * @see _.forEachRight
  1922	   * @example
  1923	   *
  1924	   * _([1, 2]).forEach(function(value) {
  1925	   *   console.log(value);
  1926	   * });
  1927	   * // => Logs `1` then `2`.
  1928	   *
  1929	   * _.forEach({ 'a': 1, 'b': 2 }, function(value, key) {
  1930	   *   console.log(key);
  1931	   * });
  1932	   * // => Logs 'a' then 'b' (iteration order is not guaranteed).
  1933	   */
  1934	  function forEach(collection, iteratee) {
  1935	    return baseEach(collection, baseIteratee(iteratee));
  1936	  }
  1937	
  1938	  /**
  1939	   * Creates an array of values by running each element in `collection` thru
  1940	   * `iteratee`. The iteratee is invoked with three arguments:
  1941	   * (value, index|key, collection).
  1942	   *
  1943	   * Many lodash methods are guarded to work as iteratees for methods like
  1944	   * `_.every`, `_.filter`, `_.map`, `_.mapValues`, `_.reject`, and `_.some`.
  1945	   *
  1946	   * The guarded methods are:
  1947	   * `ary`, `chunk`, `curry`, `curryRight`, `drop`, `dropRight`, `every`,
  1948	   * `fill`, `invert`, `parseInt`, `random`, `range`, `rangeRight`, `repeat`,
  1949	   * `sampleSize`, `slice`, `some`, `sortBy`, `split`, `take`, `takeRight`,
  1950	   * `template`, `trim`, `trimEnd`, `trimStart`, and `words`
  1951	   *
  1952	   * @static
  1953	   * @memberOf _
  1954	   * @since 0.1.0
  1955	   * @category Collection
  1956	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to iterate over.
  1957	   * @param {Array|Function|Object|string} [iteratee=_.identity]
  1958	   *  The function invoked per iteration.
  1959	   * @returns {Array} Returns the new mapped array.
  1960	   * @example
  1961	   *
  1962	   * function square(n) {
  1963	   *   return n * n;
  1964	   * }
  1965	   *
  1966	   * _.map([4, 8], square);
  1967	   * // => [16, 64]
  1968	   *
  1969	   * _.map({ 'a': 4, 'b': 8 }, square);
  1970	   * // => [16, 64] (iteration order is not guaranteed)
  1971	   *
  1972	   * var users = [
  1973	   *   { 'user': 'barney' },
  1974	   *   { 'user': 'fred' }
  1975	   * ];
  1976	   *
  1977	   * // The `_.property` iteratee shorthand.
  1978	   * _.map(users, 'user');
  1979	   * // => ['barney', 'fred']
  1980	   */
  1981	  function map(collection, iteratee) {
  1982	    return baseMap(collection, baseIteratee(iteratee));
  1983	  }
  1984	
  1985	  /**
  1986	   * Reduces `collection` to a value which is the accumulated result of running
  1987	   * each element in `collection` thru `iteratee`, where each successive
  1988	   * invocation is supplied the return value of the previous. If `accumulator`
  1989	   * is not given, the first element of `collection` is used as the initial
  1990	   * value. The iteratee is invoked with four arguments:
  1991	   * (accumulator, value, index|key, collection).
  1992	   *
  1993	   * Many lodash methods are guarded to work as iteratees for methods like
  1994	   * `_.reduce`, `_.reduceRight`, and `_.transform`.
  1995	   *
  1996	   * The guarded methods are:
  1997	   * `assign`, `defaults`, `defaultsDeep`, `includes`, `merge`, `orderBy`,
  1998	   * and `sortBy`
  1999	   *
  2000	   * @static
  2001	   * @memberOf _
  2002	   * @since 0.1.0
  2003	   * @category Collection
  2004	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to iterate over.
  2005	   * @param {Function} [iteratee=_.identity] The function invoked per iteration.
  2006	   * @param {*} [accumulator] The initial value.
  2007	   * @returns {*} Returns the accumulated value.
  2008	   * @see _.reduceRight
  2009	   * @example
  2010	   *
  2011	   * _.reduce([1, 2], function(sum, n) {
  2012	   *   return sum + n;
  2013	   * }, 0);
  2014	   * // => 3
  2015	   *
  2016	   * _.reduce({ 'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 1 }, function(result, value, key) {
  2017	   *   (result[value] || (result[value] = [])).push(key);
  2018	   *   return result;
  2019	   * }, {});
  2020	   * // => { '1': ['a', 'c'], '2': ['b'] } (iteration order is not guaranteed)
  2021	   */
  2022	  function reduce(collection, iteratee, accumulator) {
  2023	    return baseReduce(collection, baseIteratee(iteratee), accumulator, arguments.length < 3, baseEach);
  2024	  }
  2025	
  2026	  /**
  2027	   * Gets the size of `collection` by returning its length for array-like
  2028	   * values or the number of own enumerable string keyed properties for objects.
  2029	   *
  2030	   * @static
  2031	   * @memberOf _
  2032	   * @since 0.1.0
  2033	   * @category Collection
  2034	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to inspect.
  2035	   * @returns {number} Returns the collection size.
  2036	   * @example
  2037	   *
  2038	   * _.size([1, 2, 3]);
  2039	   * // => 3
  2040	   *
  2041	   * _.size({ 'a': 1, 'b': 2 });
  2042	   * // => 2
  2043	   *
  2044	   * _.size('pebbles');
  2045	   * // => 7
  2046	   */
  2047	  function size(collection) {
  2048	    if (collection == null) {
  2049	      return 0;
  2050	    }
  2051	    collection = isArrayLike(collection) ? collection : keys(collection);
  2052	    return collection.length;
  2053	  }

  2055	  /**
  2056	   * Checks if `predicate` returns truthy for **any** element of `collection`.
  2057	   * Iteration is stopped once `predicate` returns truthy. The predicate is
  2058	   * invoked with three arguments: (value, index|key, collection).
  2059	   *
  2060	   * @static
  2061	   * @memberOf _
  2062	   * @since 0.1.0

  2065	   * @param {Array|Function|Object|string} [predicate=_.identity]

  2068	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if any element passes the predicate check,
  2069	   *  else `false`.
  2070	   * @example
  2071	   *
  2072	   * _.some([null, 0, 'yes', false], Boolean);
  2073	   * // => true
  2074	   *
  2075	   * var users = [
  2076	   *   { 'user': 'barney', 'active': true },
  2077	   *   { 'user': 'fred',   'active': false }
  2078	   * ];
  2079	   *
  2080	   * // The `_.matches` iteratee shorthand.
  2081	   * _.some(users, { 'user': 'barney', 'active': false });
  2082	   * // => false
  2083	   *
  2084	   * // The `_.matchesProperty` iteratee shorthand.

  2089	   * _.some(users, 'active');

  2092	  function some(collection, predicate, guard) {

  2095	  }
  2096	
  2097	  /**
  2098	   * Creates an array of elements, sorted in ascending order by the results of
  2099	   * running each element in a collection thru each iteratee. This method
  2100	   * performs a stable sort, that is, it preserves the original sort order of
  2101	   * equal elements. The iteratees are invoked with one argument: (value).
  2102	   *
  2103	   * @static
  2104	   * @memberOf _
  2105	   * @since 0.1.0
  2106	   * @category Collection
  2107	   * @param {Array|Object} collection The collection to iterate over.
  2108	   * @param {...(Array|Array[]|Function|Function[]|Object|Object[]|string|string[])}
  2109	   *  [iteratees=[_.identity]] The iteratees to sort by.
  2110	   * @returns {Array} Returns the new sorted array.
  2111	   * @example
  2112	   *
  2113	   * var users = [
  2114	   *   { 'user': 'fred',   'age': 48 },
  2115	   *   { 'user': 'barney', 'age': 36 },
  2116	   *   { 'user': 'fred',   'age': 40 },
  2117	   *   { 'user': 'barney', 'age': 34 }
  2118	   * ];
  2119	   *
  2120	   * _.sortBy(users, function(o) { return o.user; });
  2121	   * // => objects for [['barney', 36], ['barney', 34], ['fred', 48], ['fred', 40]]
  2122	   *
  2123	   * _.sortBy(users, ['user', 'age']);
  2124	   * // => objects for [['barney', 34], ['barney', 36], ['fred', 40], ['fred', 48]]
  2125	   *
  2126	   * _.sortBy(users, 'user', function(o) {
  2127	   *   return Math.floor(o.age / 10);
  2128	   * });
  2129	   * // => objects for [['barney', 36], ['barney', 34], ['fred', 48], ['fred', 40]]
  2130	   */
  2131	  function sortBy(collection, iteratee) {
  2132	    var index = 0;
  2133	    iteratee = baseIteratee(iteratee);
  2134	
  2135	    return baseMap(baseMap(collection, function(value, key, collection) {
  2136	      return { 'value': value, 'index': index++, 'criteria': iteratee(value, key, collection) };
  2137	    }).sort(function(object, other) {
  2138	      return compareAscending(object.criteria, other.criteria) || (object.index - other.index);
  2139	    }), baseProperty('value'));
  2140	  }

  2143	
  2144	  /**
  2145	   * Creates a function that invokes `func`, with the `this` binding and arguments
  2146	   * of the created function, while it's called less than `n` times. Subsequent
  2147	   * calls to the created function return the result of the last `func` invocation.
  2148	   *
  2149	   * @static
  2150	   * @memberOf _
  2151	   * @since 3.0.0
  2152	   * @category Function
  2153	   * @param {number} n The number of calls at which `func` is no longer invoked.
  2154	   * @param {Function} func The function to restrict.
  2155	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new restricted function.
  2156	   * @example
  2157	   *
  2158	   * jQuery(element).on('click', _.before(5, addContactToList));
  2159	   * // => allows adding up to 4 contacts to the list
  2160	   */
  2161	  function before(n, func) {
  2162	    var result;
  2163	    if (typeof func != 'function') {
  2164	      throw new TypeError(FUNC_ERROR_TEXT);
  2165	    }
  2166	    n = toInteger(n);
  2167	    return function() {
  2168	      if (--n > 0) {
  2169	        result = func.apply(this, arguments);
  2170	      }
  2171	      if (n <= 1) {
  2172	        func = undefined;
  2173	      }
  2174	      return result;
  2175	    };
  2176	  }
  2177	
  2178	  /**
  2179	   * Creates a function that invokes `func` with the `this` binding of `thisArg`
  2180	   * and `partials` prepended to the arguments it receives.
  2181	   *
  2182	   * The `_.bind.placeholder` value, which defaults to `_` in monolithic builds,
  2183	   * may be used as a placeholder for partially applied arguments.
  2184	   *
  2185	   * **Note:** Unlike native `Function#bind` this method doesn't set the "length"
  2186	   * property of bound functions.
  2187	   *
  2188	   * @static
  2189	   * @memberOf _
  2190	   * @since 0.1.0
  2191	   * @category Function
  2192	   * @param {Function} func The function to bind.
  2193	   * @param {*} thisArg The `this` binding of `func`.
  2194	   * @param {...*} [partials] The arguments to be partially applied.
  2195	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new bound function.
  2196	   * @example
  2197	   *
  2198	   * var greet = function(greeting, punctuation) {
  2199	   *   return greeting + ' ' + this.user + punctuation;
  2200	   * };
  2201	   *
  2202	   * var object = { 'user': 'fred' };
  2203	   *
  2204	   * var bound = _.bind(greet, object, 'hi');
  2205	   * bound('!');
  2206	   * // => 'hi fred!'
  2207	   *
  2208	   * // Bound with placeholders.
  2209	   * var bound = _.bind(greet, object, _, '!');
  2210	   * bound('hi');
  2211	   * // => 'hi fred!'
  2212	   */
  2213	  var bind = rest(function(func, thisArg, partials) {
  2214	    return createPartialWrapper(func, BIND_FLAG | PARTIAL_FLAG, thisArg, partials);
  2215	  });
  2216	
  2217	  /**
  2218	   * Defers invoking the `func` until the current call stack has cleared. Any
  2219	   * additional arguments are provided to `func` when it's invoked.
  2220	   *
  2221	   * @static
  2222	   * @memberOf _
  2223	   * @since 0.1.0
  2224	   * @category Function
  2225	   * @param {Function} func The function to defer.
  2226	   * @param {...*} [args] The arguments to invoke `func` with.
  2227	   * @returns {number} Returns the timer id.
  2228	   * @example
  2229	   *
  2230	   * _.defer(function(text) {
  2231	   *   console.log(text);
  2232	   * }, 'deferred');
  2233	   * // => Logs 'deferred' after one or more milliseconds.
  2234	   */
  2235	  var defer = rest(function(func, args) {
  2236	    return baseDelay(func, 1, args);
  2237	  });
  2238	
  2239	  /**
  2240	   * Invokes `func` after `wait` milliseconds. Any additional arguments are
  2241	   * provided to `func` when it's invoked.
  2242	   *
  2243	   * @static
  2244	   * @memberOf _
  2245	   * @since 0.1.0
  2246	   * @category Function
  2247	   * @param {Function} func The function to delay.
  2248	   * @param {number} wait The number of milliseconds to delay invocation.
  2249	   * @param {...*} [args] The arguments to invoke `func` with.
  2250	   * @returns {number} Returns the timer id.
  2251	   * @example
  2252	   *
  2253	   * _.delay(function(text) {
  2254	   *   console.log(text);
  2255	   * }, 1000, 'later');
  2256	   * // => Logs 'later' after one second.
  2257	   */
  2258	  var delay = rest(function(func, wait, args) {
  2259	    return baseDelay(func, toNumber(wait) || 0, args);
  2260	  });
  2261	
  2262	  /**
  2263	   * Creates a function that negates the result of the predicate `func`. The
  2264	   * `func` predicate is invoked with the `this` binding and arguments of the
  2265	   * created function.
  2266	   *
  2267	   * @static
  2268	   * @memberOf _
  2269	   * @since 3.0.0
  2270	   * @category Function
  2271	   * @param {Function} predicate The predicate to negate.
  2272	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new negated function.
  2273	   * @example
  2274	   *
  2275	   * function isEven(n) {
  2276	   *   return n % 2 == 0;
  2277	   * }
  2278	   *
  2279	   * _.filter([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], _.negate(isEven));
  2280	   * // => [1, 3, 5]
  2281	   */
  2282	  function negate(predicate) {
  2283	    if (typeof predicate != 'function') {
  2284	      throw new TypeError(FUNC_ERROR_TEXT);
  2285	    }
  2286	    return function() {
  2287	      return !predicate.apply(this, arguments);
  2288	    };
  2289	  }
  2290	
  2291	  /**
  2292	   * Creates a function that is restricted to invoking `func` once. Repeat calls
  2293	   * to the function return the value of the first invocation. The `func` is
  2294	   * invoked with the `this` binding and arguments of the created function.
  2295	   *
  2296	   * @static
  2297	   * @memberOf _
  2298	   * @since 0.1.0
  2299	   * @category Function
  2300	   * @param {Function} func The function to restrict.
  2301	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new restricted function.
  2302	   * @example
  2303	   *
  2304	   * var initialize = _.once(createApplication);
  2305	   * initialize();
  2306	   * initialize();
  2307	   * // `initialize` invokes `createApplication` once
  2308	   */
  2309	  function once(func) {
  2310	    return before(2, func);
  2311	  }
  2312	
  2313	  /**
  2314	   * Creates a function that invokes `func` with the `this` binding of the
  2315	   * created function and arguments from `start` and beyond provided as
  2316	   * an array.
  2317	   *
  2318	   * **Note:** This method is based on the
  2319	   * [rest parameter](https://mdn.io/rest_parameters).
  2320	   *
  2321	   * @static
  2322	   * @memberOf _
  2323	   * @since 4.0.0
  2324	   * @category Function
  2325	   * @param {Function} func The function to apply a rest parameter to.
  2326	   * @param {number} [start=func.length-1] The start position of the rest parameter.
  2327	   * @returns {Function} Returns the new function.
  2328	   * @example
  2329	   *
  2330	   * var say = _.rest(function(what, names) {
  2331	   *   return what + ' ' + _.initial(names).join(', ') +
  2332	   *     (_.size(names) > 1 ? ', & ' : '') + _.last(names);
  2333	   * });
  2334	   *
  2335	   * say('hello', 'fred', 'barney', 'pebbles');
  2336	   * // => 'hello fred, barney, & pebbles'
  2337	   */
  2338	  function rest(func, start) {
  2339	    if (typeof func != 'function') {
  2340	      throw new TypeError(FUNC_ERROR_TEXT);
  2341	    }
  2342	    start = nativeMax(start === undefined ? (func.length - 1) : toInteger(start), 0);
  2343	    return function() {
  2344	      var args = arguments,
  2345	          index = -1,
  2346	          length = nativeMax(args.length - start, 0),
  2347	          array = Array(length);
  2348	
  2349	      while (++index < length) {
  2350	        array[index] = args[start + index];
  2351	      }
  2352	      var otherArgs = Array(start + 1);
  2353	      index = -1;
  2354	      while (++index < start) {
  2355	        otherArgs[index] = args[index];
  2356	      }
  2357	      otherArgs[start] = array;
  2358	      return func.apply(this, otherArgs);
  2359	    };
  2360	  }
  2361	
  2362	  /*------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
  2363	
  2364	  /**
  2365	   * Creates a shallow clone of `value`.
  2366	   *
  2367	   * **Note:** This method is loosely based on the
  2368	   * [structured clone algorithm](https://mdn.io/Structured_clone_algorithm)
  2369	   * and supports cloning arrays, array buffers, booleans, date objects, maps,
  2370	   * numbers, `Object` objects, regexes, sets, strings, symbols, and typed
  2371	   * arrays. The own enumerable properties of `arguments` objects are cloned
  2372	   * as plain objects. An empty object is returned for uncloneable values such
  2373	   * as error objects, functions, DOM nodes, and WeakMaps.
  2374	   *
  2375	   * @static
  2376	   * @memberOf _
  2377	   * @since 0.1.0
  2378	   * @category Lang
  2379	   * @param {*} value The value to clone.
  2380	   * @returns {*} Returns the cloned value.
  2381	   * @see _.cloneDeep
  2382	   * @example
  2383	   *
  2384	   * var objects = [{ 'a': 1 }, { 'b': 2 }];
  2385	   *
  2386	   * var shallow = _.clone(objects);
  2387	   * console.log(shallow[0] === objects[0]);
  2388	   * // => true
  2389	   */
  2390	  function clone(value) {
  2391	    if (!isObject(value)) {
  2392	      return value;
  2393	    }
  2394	    return isArray(value) ? copyArray(value) : copyObject(value, keys(value));
  2395	  }
  2396	
  2397	  /**
  2398	   * Performs a
  2399	   * [`SameValueZero`](http://ecma-international.org/ecma-262/6.0/#sec-samevaluezero)
  2400	   * comparison between two values to determine if they are equivalent.
  2401	   *
  2402	   * @static
  2403	   * @memberOf _
  2404	   * @since 4.0.0
  2405	   * @category Lang
  2406	   * @param {*} value The value to compare.
  2407	   * @param {*} other The other value to compare.
  2408	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if the values are equivalent, else `false`.
  2409	   * @example
  2410	   *
  2411	   * var object = { 'user': 'fred' };
  2412	   * var other = { 'user': 'fred' };
  2413	   *
  2414	   * _.eq(object, object);
  2415	   * // => true
  2416	   *
  2417	   * _.eq(object, other);
  2418	   * // => false
  2419	   *
  2420	   * _.eq('a', 'a');
  2421	   * // => true
  2422	   *
  2423	   * _.eq('a', Object('a'));
  2424	   * // => false
  2425	   *
  2426	   * _.eq(NaN, NaN);
  2427	   * // => true
  2428	   */
  2429	  function eq(value, other) {
  2430	    return value === other || (value !== value && other !== other);
  2431	  }
  2432	
  2433	  /**
  2434	   * Checks if `value` is likely an `arguments` object.
  2435	   *
  2436	   * @static
  2437	   * @memberOf _
  2438	   * @since 0.1.0
  2439	   * @category Lang
  2440	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2441	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is correctly classified,
  2442	   *  else `false`.
  2443	   * @example
  2444	   *
  2445	   * _.isArguments(function() { return arguments; }());
  2446	   * // => true
  2447	   *
  2448	   * _.isArguments([1, 2, 3]);
  2449	   * // => false
  2450	   */
  2451	  function isArguments(value) {
  2452	    // Safari 8.1 incorrectly makes `arguments.callee` enumerable in strict mode.
  2453	    return isArrayLikeObject(value) && hasOwnProperty.call(value, 'callee') &&
  2454	      (!propertyIsEnumerable.call(value, 'callee') || objectToString.call(value) == argsTag);
  2455	  }
  2456	
  2457	  /**
  2458	   * Checks if `value` is classified as an `Array` object.
  2459	   *
  2460	   * @static
  2461	   * @memberOf _
  2462	   * @since 0.1.0
  2463	   * @type {Function}
  2464	   * @category Lang
  2465	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2466	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is correctly classified,
  2467	   *  else `false`.
  2468	   * @example
  2469	   *
  2470	   * _.isArray([1, 2, 3]);
  2471	   * // => true
  2472	   *
  2473	   * _.isArray(document.body.children);
  2474	   * // => false
  2475	   *
  2476	   * _.isArray('abc');
  2477	   * // => false
  2478	   *
  2479	   * _.isArray(_.noop);
  2480	   * // => false
  2481	   */
  2482	  var isArray = Array.isArray;
  2483	
  2484	  /**
  2485	   * Checks if `value` is array-like. A value is considered array-like if it's
  2486	   * not a function and has a `value.length` that's an integer greater than or
  2487	   * equal to `0` and less than or equal to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.
  2488	   *
  2489	   * @static
  2490	   * @memberOf _
  2491	   * @since 4.0.0
  2492	   * @category Lang
  2493	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2494	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is array-like, else `false`.
  2495	   * @example
  2496	   *
  2497	   * _.isArrayLike([1, 2, 3]);
  2498	   * // => true
  2499	   *
  2500	   * _.isArrayLike(document.body.children);
  2501	   * // => true
  2502	   *
  2503	   * _.isArrayLike('abc');
  2504	   * // => true
  2505	   *
  2506	   * _.isArrayLike(_.noop);
  2507	   * // => false
  2508	   */
  2509	  function isArrayLike(value) {
  2510	    return value != null && isLength(getLength(value)) && !isFunction(value);
  2511	  }
  2512	
  2513	  /**
  2514	   * This method is like `_.isArrayLike` except that it also checks if `value`
  2515	   * is an object.
  2516	   *
  2517	   * @static
  2518	   * @memberOf _
  2519	   * @since 4.0.0
  2520	   * @category Lang
  2521	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2522	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is an array-like object,
  2523	   *  else `false`.
  2524	   * @example
  2525	   *
  2526	   * _.isArrayLikeObject([1, 2, 3]);
  2527	   * // => true
  2528	   *
  2529	   * _.isArrayLikeObject(document.body.children);
  2530	   * // => true
  2531	   *
  2532	   * _.isArrayLikeObject('abc');
  2533	   * // => false
  2534	   *
  2535	   * _.isArrayLikeObject(_.noop);
  2536	   * // => false
  2537	   */
  2538	  function isArrayLikeObject(value) {
  2539	    return isObjectLike(value) && isArrayLike(value);
  2540	  }
  2541	
  2542	  /**
  2543	   * Checks if `value` is classified as a boolean primitive or object.
  2544	   *
  2545	   * @static
  2546	   * @memberOf _
  2547	   * @since 0.1.0
  2548	   * @category Lang
  2549	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2550	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is correctly classified,
  2551	   *  else `false`.
  2552	   * @example
  2553	   *
  2554	   * _.isBoolean(false);
  2555	   * // => true
  2556	   *
  2557	   * _.isBoolean(null);
  2558	   * // => false
  2559	   */
  2560	  function isBoolean(value) {
  2561	    return value === true || value === false ||
  2562	      (isObjectLike(value) && objectToString.call(value) == boolTag);
  2563	  }
  2564	
  2565	  /**
  2566	   * Checks if `value` is classified as a `Date` object.
  2567	   *
  2568	   * @static
  2569	   * @memberOf _
  2570	   * @since 0.1.0
  2571	   * @category Lang
  2572	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2573	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is correctly classified,
  2574	   *  else `false`.
  2575	   * @example
  2576	   *
  2577	   * _.isDate(new Date);
  2578	   * // => true
  2579	   *
  2580	   * _.isDate('Mon April 23 2012');
  2581	   * // => false
  2582	   */
  2583	  function isDate(value) {
  2584	    return isObjectLike(value) && objectToString.call(value) == dateTag;
  2585	  }
  2586	
  2587	  /**
  2588	   * Checks if `value` is an empty object, collection, map, or set.
  2589	   *
  2590	   * Objects are considered empty if they have no own enumerable string keyed
  2591	   * properties.
  2592	   *
  2593	   * Array-like values such as `arguments` objects, arrays, buffers, strings, or
  2594	   * jQuery-like collections are considered empty if they have a `length` of `0`.
  2595	   * Similarly, maps and sets are considered empty if they have a `size` of `0`.
  2596	   *
  2597	   * @static
  2598	   * @memberOf _
  2599	   * @since 0.1.0
  2600	   * @category Lang
  2601	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2602	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is empty, else `false`.
  2603	   * @example
  2604	   *
  2605	   * _.isEmpty(null);
  2606	   * // => true
  2607	   *
  2608	   * _.isEmpty(true);
  2609	   * // => true
  2610	   *
  2611	   * _.isEmpty(1);
  2612	   * // => true
  2613	   *
  2614	   * _.isEmpty([1, 2, 3]);
  2615	   * // => false
  2616	   *
  2617	   * _.isEmpty({ 'a': 1 });
  2618	   * // => false
  2619	   */
  2620	  function isEmpty(value) {
  2621	    if (isArrayLike(value) &&
  2622	        (isArray(value) || isString(value) ||
  2623	          isFunction(value.splice) || isArguments(value))) {
  2624	      return !value.length;
  2625	    }
  2626	    return !keys(value).length;
  2627	  }
  2628	
  2629	  /**
  2630	   * Performs a deep comparison between two values to determine if they are
  2631	   * equivalent.
  2632	   *
  2633	   * **Note:** This method supports comparing arrays, array buffers, booleans,
  2634	   * date objects, error objects, maps, numbers, `Object` objects, regexes,
  2635	   * sets, strings, symbols, and typed arrays. `Object` objects are compared
  2636	   * by their own, not inherited, enumerable properties. Functions and DOM
  2637	   * nodes are **not** supported.
  2638	   *
  2639	   * @static
  2640	   * @memberOf _
  2641	   * @since 0.1.0
  2642	   * @category Lang
  2643	   * @param {*} value The value to compare.
  2644	   * @param {*} other The other value to compare.
  2645	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if the values are equivalent,
  2646	   *  else `false`.
  2647	   * @example
  2648	   *
  2649	   * var object = { 'user': 'fred' };
  2650	   * var other = { 'user': 'fred' };
  2651	   *
  2652	   * _.isEqual(object, other);
  2653	   * // => true
  2654	   *
  2655	   * object === other;
  2656	   * // => false
  2657	   */
  2658	  function isEqual(value, other) {
  2659	    return baseIsEqual(value, other);
  2660	  }
  2661	
  2662	  /**
  2663	   * Checks if `value` is a finite primitive number.
  2664	   *
  2665	   * **Note:** This method is based on
  2666	   * [`Number.isFinite`](https://mdn.io/Number/isFinite).
  2667	   *
  2668	   * @static
  2669	   * @memberOf _
  2670	   * @since 0.1.0
  2671	   * @category Lang
  2672	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2673	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is a finite number,
  2674	   *  else `false`.
  2675	   * @example
  2676	   *
  2677	   * _.isFinite(3);
  2678	   * // => true
  2679	   *
  2680	   * _.isFinite(Number.MIN_VALUE);
  2681	   * // => true
  2682	   *
  2683	   * _.isFinite(Infinity);
  2684	   * // => false
  2685	   *
  2686	   * _.isFinite('3');
  2687	   * // => false
  2688	   */
  2689	  function isFinite(value) {
  2690	    return typeof value == 'number' && nativeIsFinite(value);
  2691	  }
  2692	
  2693	  /**
  2694	   * Checks if `value` is classified as a `Function` object.
  2695	   *
  2696	   * @static
  2697	   * @memberOf _
  2698	   * @since 0.1.0
  2699	   * @category Lang
  2700	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2701	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is correctly classified,
  2702	   *  else `false`.
  2703	   * @example
  2704	   *
  2705	   * _.isFunction(_);
  2706	   * // => true
  2707	   *
  2708	   * _.isFunction(/abc/);
  2709	   * // => false
  2710	   */
  2711	  function isFunction(value) {
  2712	    // The use of `Object#toString` avoids issues with the `typeof` operator
  2713	    // in Safari 8 which returns 'object' for typed array and weak map constructors,
  2714	    // and PhantomJS 1.9 which returns 'function' for `NodeList` instances.
  2715	    var tag = isObject(value) ? objectToString.call(value) : '';
  2716	    return tag == funcTag || tag == genTag;
  2717	  }
  2718	
  2719	  /**
  2720	   * Checks if `value` is a valid array-like length.
  2721	   *
  2722	   * **Note:** This function is loosely based on
  2723	   * [`ToLength`](http://ecma-international.org/ecma-262/6.0/#sec-tolength).
  2724	   *
  2725	   * @static
  2726	   * @memberOf _
  2727	   * @since 4.0.0
  2728	   * @category Lang
  2729	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2730	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is a valid length,
  2731	   *  else `false`.
  2732	   * @example
  2733	   *
  2734	   * _.isLength(3);
  2735	   * // => true
  2736	   *
  2737	   * _.isLength(Number.MIN_VALUE);
  2738	   * // => false
  2739	   *
  2740	   * _.isLength(Infinity);
  2741	   * // => false
  2742	   *
  2743	   * _.isLength('3');
  2744	   * // => false
  2745	   */
  2746	  function isLength(value) {
  2747	    return typeof value == 'number' &&
  2748	      value > -1 && value % 1 == 0 && value <= MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
  2749	  }
  2750	
  2751	  /**
  2752	   * Checks if `value` is the
  2753	   * [language type](http://www.ecma-international.org/ecma-262/6.0/#sec-ecmascript-language-types)
  2754	   * of `Object`. (e.g. arrays, functions, objects, regexes, `new Number(0)`, and `new String('')`)
  2755	   *
  2756	   * @static
  2757	   * @memberOf _
  2758	   * @since 0.1.0
  2759	   * @category Lang
  2760	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2761	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is an object, else `false`.
  2762	   * @example
  2763	   *
  2764	   * _.isObject({});
  2765	   * // => true
  2766	   *
  2767	   * _.isObject([1, 2, 3]);
  2768	   * // => true
  2769	   *
  2770	   * _.isObject(_.noop);
  2771	   * // => true
  2772	   *
  2773	   * _.isObject(null);
  2774	   * // => false
  2775	   */
  2776	  function isObject(value) {
  2777	    var type = typeof value;
  2778	    return !!value && (type == 'object' || type == 'function');
  2779	  }
  2780	
  2781	  /**
  2782	   * Checks if `value` is object-like. A value is object-like if it's not `null`
  2783	   * and has a `typeof` result of "object".
  2784	   *
  2785	   * @static
  2786	   * @memberOf _
  2787	   * @since 4.0.0
  2788	   * @category Lang
  2789	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2790	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is object-like, else `false`.
  2791	   * @example
  2792	   *
  2793	   * _.isObjectLike({});
  2794	   * // => true
  2795	   *
  2796	   * _.isObjectLike([1, 2, 3]);
  2797	   * // => true
  2798	   *
  2799	   * _.isObjectLike(_.noop);
  2800	   * // => false
  2801	   *
  2802	   * _.isObjectLike(null);
  2803	   * // => false
  2804	   */
  2805	  function isObjectLike(value) {
  2806	    return !!value && typeof value == 'object';
  2807	  }
  2808	
  2809	  /**
  2810	   * Checks if `value` is `NaN`.
  2811	   *
  2812	   * **Note:** This method is based on
  2813	   * [`Number.isNaN`](https://mdn.io/Number/isNaN) and is not the same as
  2814	   * global [`isNaN`](https://mdn.io/isNaN) which returns `true` for
  2815	   * `undefined` and other non-number values.
  2816	   *
  2817	   * @static
  2818	   * @memberOf _
  2819	   * @since 0.1.0
  2820	   * @category Lang
  2821	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2822	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is `NaN`, else `false`.
  2823	   * @example
  2824	   *
  2825	   * _.isNaN(NaN);
  2826	   * // => true
  2827	   *
  2828	   * _.isNaN(new Number(NaN));
  2829	   * // => true
  2830	   *
  2831	   * isNaN(undefined);
  2832	   * // => true
  2833	   *
  2834	   * _.isNaN(undefined);
  2835	   * // => false
  2836	   */
  2837	  function isNaN(value) {
  2838	    // An `NaN` primitive is the only value that is not equal to itself.
  2839	    // Perform the `toStringTag` check first to avoid errors with some
  2840	    // ActiveX objects in IE.
  2841	    return isNumber(value) && value != +value;
  2842	  }
  2843	
  2844	  /**
  2845	   * Checks if `value` is `null`.
  2846	   *
  2847	   * @static
  2848	   * @memberOf _
  2849	   * @since 0.1.0
  2850	   * @category Lang
  2851	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2852	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is `null`, else `false`.
  2853	   * @example
  2854	   *
  2855	   * _.isNull(null);
  2856	   * // => true
  2857	   *
  2858	   * _.isNull(void 0);
  2859	   * // => false
  2860	   */
  2861	  function isNull(value) {
  2862	    return value === null;
  2863	  }
  2864	
  2865	  /**
  2866	   * Checks if `value` is classified as a `Number` primitive or object.
  2867	   *
  2868	   * **Note:** To exclude `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, and `NaN`, which are
  2869	   * classified as numbers, use the `_.isFinite` method.
  2870	   *
  2871	   * @static
  2872	   * @memberOf _
  2873	   * @since 0.1.0
  2874	   * @category Lang
  2875	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2876	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is correctly classified,
  2877	   *  else `false`.
  2878	   * @example
  2879	   *
  2880	   * _.isNumber(3);
  2881	   * // => true
  2882	   *
  2883	   * _.isNumber(Number.MIN_VALUE);
  2884	   * // => true
  2885	   *
  2886	   * _.isNumber(Infinity);
  2887	   * // => true
  2888	   *
  2889	   * _.isNumber('3');
  2890	   * // => false
  2891	   */
  2892	  function isNumber(value) {
  2893	    return typeof value == 'number' ||
  2894	      (isObjectLike(value) && objectToString.call(value) == numberTag);
  2895	  }
  2896	
  2897	  /**
  2898	   * Checks if `value` is classified as a `RegExp` object.
  2899	   *
  2900	   * @static
  2901	   * @memberOf _
  2902	   * @since 0.1.0
  2903	   * @category Lang
  2904	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2905	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is correctly classified,
  2906	   *  else `false`.
  2907	   * @example
  2908	   *

  2910	   * // => true
  2911	   *
  2912	   * _.isRegExp('/abc/');
  2913	   * // => false
  2914	   */
  2915	  function isRegExp(value) {
  2916	    return isObject(value) && objectToString.call(value) == regexpTag;
  2917	  }
  2918	
  2919	  /**
  2920	   * Checks if `value` is classified as a `String` primitive or object.
  2921	   *
  2922	   * @static
  2923	   * @since 0.1.0
  2924	   * @memberOf _
  2925	   * @category Lang
  2926	   * @param {*} value The value to check.
  2927	   * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is correctly classified,
  2928	   *  else `false`.
  2929	   * @example
  2930	   *

  2932	   * // => true
  2933	   *
  2934	   * _.isString(1);
  2935	   * // => false
  2936	   */
  2937	  function isString(value) {
  2938	    return typeof value == 'string' ||
  2939	      (!isArray(value) && isObjectLike(value) && objectToString.call(value) == stringTag);
  2940	  }

  2945	   * @static
  2946	   * @since 0.1.0

  2963	  /**
  2964	   * Converts `value` to an array.
  2965	   *
  2966	   * @static
  2967	   * @since 0.1.0
  2968	   * @memberOf _
  2969	   * @category Lang
  2970	   * @param {*} value The value to convert.
  2971	   * @returns {Array} Returns the converted array.
  2972	   * @example
  2973	   *
  2974	   * _.toArray({ 'a': 1, 'b': 2 });
  2975	   * // => [1, 2]
  2976	   *

  2979	   *

  2981	   * // => []
  2982	   *
  2983	   * _.toArray(null);
  2984	   * // => []

  2986	  function toArray(value) {
  2987	    if (!isArrayLike(value)) {
  2988	      return values(value);
  2989	    }
  2990	    return value.length ? copyArray(value) : [];
  2991	  }

  3044	  var toNumber = Number;

  3046	  /**
  3047	   * Converts `value` to a string. An empty string is returned for `null`
  3048	   * and `undefined` values. The sign of `-0` is preserved.
  3049	   *
  3050	   * @static
  3051	   * @memberOf _
  3052	   * @since 4.0.0
  3053	   * @category Lang
  3054	   * @param {*} value The value to process.
  3055	   * @returns {string} Returns the string.
  3056	   * @example
  3057	   *
  3058	   * _.toString(null);
  3059	   * // => ''
  3060	   *
  3061	   * _.toString(-0);
  3062	   * // => '-0'
  3063	   *
  3064	   * _.toString([1, 2, 3]);
  3065	   * // => '1,2,3'
  3066	   */
  3067	  function toString(value) {
  3068	    if (typeof value == 'string') {
  3069	      return value;
  3070	    }
  3071	    return value == null ? '' : (value + '');
  3072	  }
